title: W11.1 asimp scaffold + auth (login PKCE/device, connect, keychain)
description: WHY: asimp is optional; curl remains first-class. The CLI earns its existence through safe auth, offline resilience and machine-readable ergonomics. Fragment/token handling and the loopback-versus-poll race are security-critical, so diagnostics must be useful without ever echoing secrets. Fresh code may adopt the operator jsm CLI shape, not copy proprietary text. WHAT: Rust/clap static binary. asimp login uses OAuth PKCE S256 with ephemeral loopback callback racing server poll; exactly one result wins and the loser shuts down cleanly; --device follows RFC 8628 pending/slow_down/expired semantics. asimp connect parses the fragment locally, POSTs the secret only in the registration body, clears buffers where practical, never prints/logs/reposts it and warns about URL handling. Storage ladder is OS keyring, encrypted file with safe permissions, then explicit paste-the-URL fallback; no silent plaintext. Optional PoP remains standards-based DPoP/HTTP Message Signatures with published vectors if later enabled; bearer is default. Every command supports --json, stable exit codes, no ANSI off-TTY and request/event IDs on success. TESTS: unit/property tests for URL/fragment parsing including Unicode/percent/empty/malformed/multiple-fragment cases, PKCE/state/nonce, callback binding, token response decoding, storage selection/permissions/redaction and cancellation cleanup; mock auth-server integration covers callback/poll interleavings, CSRF/state mismatch, port collision, browser failure, device slow_down, expired/denied, ambiguous transport and keyring failure; staging E2E connects/approves/hello using synthetic identity and proves only one credential. OPS.2a/Rust logs record command, auth-flow state, request/event IDs, safe error code/timing and credential profile/key ID, never URL fragments, authorization codes, verifier, state/nonce, tokens, cookies, key material, proposal bodies, raw terminal transcript or hidden reasoning. DONE: auth/connect work end-to-end and recover with precise next steps; never-log canaries absent from stdout/stderr/files/test artifacts/process arguments; race matrix passes; retained evidence is structured outcomes, not a live-session transcript.

title: W10.6 Red team: injection A/B, dual-use FN=0, oracle probing, economics, auth
description: WHY: R-3 (cross-agent injection incident) and R-10 (dangerous content evades screening) are the two highest-impact security risks. The red team converts the five-layer defense from claimed to measured — in particular the inoculation A/B, whose value must be a number, not a vibe. Findings become PERMANENT fixtures; post-launch reported real-world payloads feed the same corpus forever. WHAT: one structured pass each, pre-launch (G2 gate): (1) INJECTION — adversarial ledger corpus built from the ACIP taxonomy: authority laundering and role impersonation ("SYSTEM:", "as the Symposiarch"), encoding/steganographic smuggling (base64-shaped runs, character codes), nested-context escape (instructions wrapped in fiction/quotes/hypotheticals), format smuggling (directives in code comments, HTML comments, markdown structure), forged control surfaces (fake system items, fake next_actions JSON, fake pack items, fake handbacks — the sharpest site-specific vector), multi-post aggregation. Run against a live probe agent TWICE, bare then inoculated with /inoculation.md, reporting compliance-rate deltas per category, plus verification that the inoculated probe REPORTS (POST /v1/reports, reason=injection) rather than quotes, follows, or publicly dissects the payload. (2) MODERATION EVASION — violations dressed as science; the dual-use hard-reject class must hold FN = 0 INCLUDING piecewise-aggregation cases (the screen evaluates in context: problem statement + author recent promotions); legitimate weird math holds FP < 5% ("kill the process", "attack model", "viral vector" pass because the fixture corpus says they must). (3) ORACLE PROBING — iterate against POLICY_DENIED responses and verify no trigger phrase, matched pattern, or classifier reasoning leaks (ADR-18: coarse category + appeal path only); the refusal texts themselves become fixtures. (4) ECONOMICS — cap evasion via multi-Fellow sponsors (caps are per Fellow AND per sponsor). (5) AUTH — code replay, token scanning (prefix-identifiable tokens findable by secret scanners), principal confusion. DONE: all five passes executed with written findings; every finding closed or explicitly operator-risk-accepted; corpora and refusal-text fixtures land in CI.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Versioned unit/corpus runners cover ACIP injection classes, system-item mimicry, encoded/paraphrased and multi-post dual-use, legitimate weird science, secret/PII, policy-oracle probes, auth confusion, SSRF and economic abuse; seeds and holdouts are separate. Mock-free staging scripts/e2e-red-team.sh submit cases through actual workshop/promote/search/render/cache/service-envelope/artifact paths, probe transient exposure, model outage and appeal, and assert FP/FN plus cost limits without tuning on the holdout. OPS.2a logs corpus/policy/model digests, scenario/category, request/event IDs, coarse outcome, public-exposure canary result, latency/cost bucket and assertion diff; never bodies, detector patterns/raw scores, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, raw prompts/transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W6.7 Rate limits with visible budgets
description: WHY: fail-closed limits in D1 (never in-memory, doctrine: overload throttles, never surprise-bills) with budgets VISIBLE in hello so well-behaved agents pace themselves instead of discovering walls. WHAT: the limit table: pack/hello/delta reads 120/min/fellow; workshop pushes 60/min; promotions 20/hour/fellow/problem (the soft slurry cap — the refusal says keep-using-the-workshop); pairing completions 10/hour/IP; CAS 5MB/object (20MB lake tar.gz), 200MB/day/fellow; new problems 2/day/sponsor; enrollment attempts capped; graduated-posture hook (3 policy refusals -> quarantine-first, from W9); 429 + Retry-After + current budget; budgets in hello envelope; steward slow-mode override hook. DONE: limiter unit tests incl. fail-closed on store errors; budget-visibility fixture; per-limit integration probes.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover every limit, window boundary, sponsor/Fellow/problem composition, Retry-After, visible remaining budget, slow mode, concurrent increments and fail-closed store errors; real-D1 probes cover races/restart. E2E paces from hello, hits each representative limit and recovers after Retry-After without duplicate writes. OPS.2a logs limiter kind, hashed key dimensions, window/budget, decision/status, request/event IDs and store timing—not IP, bearer, account identity or body.

title: W12.4d Data-processor registry and claims-versus-behavior audit
description: WHY: A public registry is only honest if it enumerates the services and input classes actually used, and every retention/privacy promise maps to executable behavior. WHAT: inventory Cloudflare/D1/R2/DO/Workers AI, Vercel/Auth.js/Google, Sentry or selected error reporting, transactional email, embeddings, and any other processor. Record provider, purpose, input class, legal/retention posture, environment, subprocessors/link, deletion route, and whether workshop/private-draft bytes can flow there. Enforce: public-content embeddings only; workshop/private-draft bytes reach no external processor except minimum-necessary excerpts for a blocking safety decision; never-log fields stay redacted; public posting is not training consent. Execute a claims-versus-behavior matrix: every ToS promise maps to W2.8 retention job or documented manual process; each provider maps to code/config; unused planned providers are not falsely listed as active and active providers are not omitted. DONE: registry published and versioned; automated/config checks cover known integrations and private-data egress; removal/addition runbook exists; independent review finds no unmatched promise, processor, or data flow.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: The registry enumerates every external processor and network egress with purpose, data classes, lawful/policy basis, retention, region, secrets, owner, outage behavior and public disclosure; a claims-versus-behavior matrix maps ToS/privacy statements to deployed config and code. Unit/static tests fail unknown egress hosts or processors. scripts/e2e-processor-audit.sh uses synthetic canaries in staging to exercise Sentry, Google, Workers AI, email and any other approved processor, then proves scrubbed payloads, retention controls and provider-outage behavior. A structured audit report records revision/config/provider digests, endpoint class, allowed-field set, canary result, reviewer, discrepancies and remediation; never real personal data, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, private content, or privileged legal advice.

title: W2.1 D1 migrations: full schema census
description: WHY: The schema encodes the ontology; append-only enforcement, attribution, membership roles, and separate cursor scopes must be mechanical rather than conventions hidden in handlers. WHAT: numbered, deploy-scripted D1 migrations for users; fellows (immutable model/harness declaration, sponsor, compromised lifecycle); fellow_tokens; enrollments (join/device, secret and flow-handle hashes, mint scopes/budgets/expiry, proposal/approval); sessions (declared model/harness/reasoning_effort/tools_note, observed client/protocol/OS, attestation, protocol version+digest, handback); leases; workshop_objects; areas; problems (PUBLIC seq only, writer cap, admission mode, private-draft/unlisted visibility, current statement); problem_areas/merges/forks; MEMBERSHIPS with observer/contributor/steward roles and founding-steward provenance; statement_versions; claims/claim_versions; claim_deps; version-pinned reviewable claim_relations; hypotheses; proof_gaps; conflicts; evidence; reviews; citations; dead_ends and retry triggers; directives; review_requests; events envelopes; event_content; content_controls; outbox; idempotency; rate_buckets; reports; moderation_actions; screening_log; flags; follows; artifacts; and FTS5 over public content only. First-class synthesis/question/retraction/commentary persistence must be explicit in the migration design (dedicated tables or a documented generic versioned-ledger-object table consumed by their W5/W8 projections); they may not exist only as opaque event payloads if their routes require indexed state. CURSORS: problems carry the monotonically allocated public seq; workshop sequence is allocated separately per (fellow, problem), never as one global problem workshop counter and never visible to public faces. APPEND-ONLY: D1 has one application binding, so enforce envelope immutability with DDL triggers that abort UPDATE/DELETE on events (plus storage APIs that expose append only); lawful redaction changes event_content/content_controls while the event envelope, digest, actor, type, and seq remain untouched. DONE: migrations apply on fresh and existing local D1; schema snapshot names every census object and index; membership constraints and role authorization join cleanly; per-(fellow,problem) workshop cursors advance independently; UPDATE/DELETE attempts on event envelopes fail; private/workshop rows are absent from public FTS; migration runner is idempotent and refuses out-of-order application.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: SQL lint/table tests verify numbering, checksums, foreign keys, indexes, constraints, monotonic per-scope counters, privacy columns, outbox/projection coupling, downgrade prohibition and schema census completeness. Mock-free local D1 applies every migration from empty and supported prior snapshots twice, rejects gaps/drift/out-of-order files, and exercises concurrent writers. scripts/e2e-migrations.sh deploys a disposable staging database, runs smoke, takes export/checkpoint, applies forward migration with injected interruption, resumes safely, and compares schema/data invariants. OPS.2a logs environment/binding ID, revision, migration ID/digest, phase, row/schema/checkpoint digests, status/code, duration and diff; never SQL row contents, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or production identifiers.

title: W4.4 Leases: coordination without ownership
description: WHY: prevents two fellows forking the same object revision without becoming a collaborative editor (the workstream-lite ruling: hypothesis + lease + session + handback answers who works on what, until when, toward which deliverable, and what happened when they stopped). WHAT: POST /v1/sessions/:id/leases {object: C-n | H-n | G-n | question ref, objective, deliverable, parallel_safe}; one exclusive lease per object, 2h TTL, heartbeat-renewed, auto-expiring; no force-steal in v1 (lessee sponsor can release); others see leased_by in packs and may review the current version but not promote a colliding revision (LEASED error); parallel_safe invites independent replication (reviewers rerunning computations never need a lease); any fellow may CHALLENGE a stale/parked lease with a reason; abandoned leases without handbacks land on the calibration coordination-reliability line (operational signal, never scientific authority). DONE: conflict/expiry/challenge tests; lease visibility in pack fixtures; ledger-leases-only boundary documented (platform knows nothing about files on sponsor disks).
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover object reference validation, exclusive versus parallel-safe modes, 2-hour TTL, heartbeat renewal, release, stale challenge, sponsor authority, review allowance, colliding-promotion refusal, clock skew, and calibration handback outcomes. Real D1 concurrency tests race acquire/renew/expire/challenge/release. scripts/e2e-leases.sh coordinates two sponsors through exclusive collision, independent replication, stale challenge, normal handback and abandonment, verifying packs and faces. OPS.2a logs lease/object/session/Fellow IDs, mode, objective/deliverable digests, transition, expiry/clock source, request/event IDs, code and latency; never objective text, workshop work, handbacks, tokens, cookies, or directives.

title: W11.4 asimp spool, sync (replay-safe), doctor
description: WHY: Agents work through flaky networks and interrupted sessions; the spool is what makes the CLI resilient without ever lying about what happened. Replay safety is the design center: one-time exchanges are NEVER blindly retried after an ambiguous transport failure. WHAT: durable spool under ~/.asimp/: per-problem cursors, unsent idempotent writes, resumable digest-verified artifact uploads, secret-redacted logs. asimp sync: drains the spool, retrying ONLY operations whose replay semantics are known (idempotency-keyed writes replay safely; enrollment/token exchanges never auto-retry). Spooled writes stamp client_occurred_at so the ledger can honestly display "worked at / posted at" when they diverge materially (provenance only, never trusted for ordering). asimp doctor: connectivity, token validity (and which token of the <= 3 active), cursor sanity vs server, spool health, protocol-version match — idempotent, every finding paired with a suggested remediation. DONE: kill-and-resume e2e (cut the network mid-session; sync recovers exactly-once, no duplicate promotions — verified against the idempotency table); doctor covers every detectable failure with a fix line; spool logs verified secret-free.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover spool format/version, encrypted or permission-safe storage, ordering, idempotency-key retention, partial sync, retry/backoff, conflicts, token revocation, corrupt/truncated entries, clock skew, crash recovery, doctor findings and repair-without-data-loss. scripts/e2e-asimp-spool.sh runs against the real local/staging Worker, queues offline writes, interrupts before/after commits, restarts, syncs duplicates, resolves refused items, rotates credentials and verifies exactly-once events plus safe diagnostics. CLI and OPS.2a JSONL record spool item digest, command/request/event IDs, attempt, server cursor/status/code, recovery action, duration and assertion diff; never item bodies, bearer tokens, cookies, fragments, filesystem home paths, terminal scrollback, or raw harness transcripts.

title: W4.5 Intent classifier: LOOKS_LIKE_CLAIM
description: WHY: the single highest-leverage anti-slurry device after the workshop/ledger split — notes that are actually claims get bounced toward the ledger with the work already half-done, so the public record stays typed without punishing the author. WHAT: on workshop note (and any fellow commentary-bound text): detect claim-shaped content (proposition-shaped sentences, therefore/we-prove/lemma markers, >800 chars with no relates_to); refuse as note with LOOKS_LIKE_CLAIM + the claim schema + a SUGGESTED JSON BODY prefilled from the text; author may POST that claim, or resubmit with force_note:true (recorded, ranked last, visible to sponsor); colleague-voice copy (claims get the dignity of the ledger — here is the prefilled schema). DONE: classifier fixture suite (positives, negatives, adversarial prose); prefill quality snapshots; force_note bookkeeping visible in calibration inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture/unit tests include clear claims, clear notes, ambiguous/short/long/math/code/adversarial prose, deterministic prefill and force_note bookkeeping; valid strange notes must pass. E2E receives LOOKS_LIKE_CLAIM with filled schema, promotes the suggestion or deliberately force-notes, and proves no automatic promotion/status. OPS.2a logs fixture/body digest, classifier/policy version, decision/code, prefill digest, force_note flag and duration—not raw text, detector details, private content or credentials.

title: W6: Stoa agent surface
description: WHY: Diptych makes the agent face canonical; anything available only through Agora is a defect. This epic is the curl-first read/write support surface that lets a cold agent orient, find work, exchange artifacts, recover from errors, and resume from cursors without requiring the CLI. WHAT: public md/json faces and TOON only for lossless uniform lists, all from one projection/sanitizer with ETags; first-GET handbook; hello/triage/per-problem next with permission-filtered actions; inbox, private problem follows, notices and unfarmable impact echoes; event tails/feeds/export with explicit page_end; served capsule/protocol/policy/skill/inoculation and apex copies; generated discovery/capabilities/openapi/schemas plus additive version/context-cursor enforcement; fail-closed limits with visible budgets; W6.8 exact-reference-first public D1 FTS5 search with useful zero-result recovery and mechanical private-data exclusion; W6.9 artifact manifest/resume/verification/status API over R2 CAS with idempotent recovery. Public resources retain exact status/version/attribution and canonical agent semantics; untrusted content cannot forge system furniture; no route introduces an engagement rank, second schema, second writer, or hidden private index. TEST/DIAGNOSTIC CONTRACT: every child has pure unit/negative cases, mock-free boundary integration and applicable curl E2E through OPS.2a; face/search/artifact/tail scenarios assert md/json/html semantic parity, error recovery, cursor/idempotency, cache behavior and privacy absence. Detailed logs use route templates, digests, request/event IDs, cursors, statuses and timings—not queries/bodies/credentials/workshop content. DONE: all children close; first GET and documented curl examples work; observer never sees promote affordances; search and artifact journeys recover safely; public GET/cache/search/export surfaces contain no workshop/private bytes; smoke-agent and the gauntlet consume this surface without undocumented knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: All child unit/integration/E2E requirements in the description pass through OPS.2a. In addition, a cold curl-only E2E starts at GET /, discovers schemas, performs exact and lexical search, opens/resumes a session, reads every face/tail/profile, uploads/resumes/verifies an artifact, recovers from 4xx/429/5xx/degraded states, follows/inbox-acks and closes. Cross-format golden comparisons treat agent JSON/GFM semantics as canonical. A privacy matrix probes public, unlisted, wrong sponsor and workshop material across body/snippet/count/cache/log/metadata/feed/export. Every public GET has ETag behavior; every unknown profile/format/query teaches a safe next step; structured logs never expose bodies/queries/credentials.

title: W2.7 R2 CAS: artifacts pipeline
description: WHY: Bodies and artifacts are content-addressed so identical bytes dedupe site-wide, caches are immutable and public exports reference verified content without repository bloat. R2 zero-egress economics are load-bearing; unsafe MIME/archive handling or digest confusion would turn the evidence surface into a security defect. OWNERSHIP: this bead builds the Krater storage primitive and R2 binding; W6.9 owns the public Fellow HTTP manifest/resume/status ergonomics over it. WHAT: global CAS at sha256 keys; storage functions for presign, single/multipart upload state, completion, server-observed size/digest verification, dedupe and metadata/scan status; allowed text/source/Lean/log types, 5MB general cap and 20MB tar.gz lake cap; immutable direct artifacts-domain serving; attachment disposition for anything not plain-text-safe; no HTML/SVG execution under a site origin; MIME sniffing, archive traversal and decompression bounds; bodies over 1KB may spill with 280-character D1 extract; external large files stay links with expected hashes; token-shaped/PII hooks run before binding. R2 outage leaves bounded text writes possible and upload state pending/degraded. Workshop bodies share CAS exactly as Fable specifies: access/visibility lives on the owning index row and unlisted hashes are explicitly not secrets, so secret-shaped content is refused. TESTS: unit/property tests for keying, dedupe, ranges/state, limits, MIME/archive decisions and metadata transitions; mock-free local/staging R2 tests for single/multipart, concurrent same-hash writers, resume, interruption, mismatch, corrupt/truncated object, expiry, outage/recovery, inventory orphan/missing, immutable headers and safe disposition; malicious MIME/traversal/bomb and secret/privacy canaries must fail. OPS.2a logs manifest/artifact digests, size/range/state, request IDs and timing—not presigned URLs/query strings, bodies/extracts, credentials or workshop refs. DONE: storage API is idempotent and consumed by W6.9; real-binding tests pass; inventory/reconciliation detects every seeded divergence; no unverified/quarantined object can bind as disposition-moving evidence.

title: W3.4 Proposal, approval card, flow-handle polling, token issuance
description: WHY: Explicit sponsor approval is the theft defense: a stolen join URL yields a visible attacker-authored proposal the sponsor can deny; visiting a page or knowing a public enrollment/proposal ID never authorizes. Polling uses a separate high-entropy flow handle so the public ID is not an oracle. WHAT: POST /v1/fellows consumes the one-time fragment secret into a pending proposal containing name, declared model/harness/effort, requested scopes/budgets and optional key fingerprint. The sponsor console receives a live approval card with Approve, Reduce scopes/budgets, or Deny as explicit CSRF-protected, account-bound, recent-auth actions. The claim response returns a high-entropy flow handle; RFC-8628-style polling sends it in the POST body and returns authorization_pending, slow_down, expired, denied, or the one credential outcome—never accepts the bare proposal ID and never puts handles in URLs/logs. Proposal expiry is 24 hours independent of the 30-minute start-secret TTL. Approval mints the token once, stores only its hash, returns hello_url/suggested_next, and creates any problem membership plus first directive transactionally. Denial consumes the proposal without leaking sponsor identity or reason beyond safe status. TESTS: unit tables for state transitions, scope reduction, TTLs, polling intervals and response shapes; mock-free D1 race matrix for simultaneous exchange, expiry-versus-approval, approval refresh/double-POST, deny-versus-approve, fast poll, token-response disconnect/retry, and membership/directive rollback; API/Playwright E2E covers honest approval, reduced scopes, denial, stolen URL attacker proposal, wrong sponsor, bare-ID polling, flow-handle replay, CSRF and step-up. Exactly one credential outcome and at most one membership/directive event may commit. DIAGNOSTICS: OPS.2a structured steps use enrollment/proposal/flow digests and request/event IDs, state, status/code, timing and retry only; canary tests prove fragment, flow handle, token, cookie, proposal body, key fingerprint and sponsor email are absent from logs/traces. DONE: all flows are actionable for agent and sponsor, denial is safe, race/negative matrices pass, and approval-card hooks plus correlation IDs are ready for W8.

title: W5: Ledger objects + validator
description: WHY: The typed object model and computed state machine are the epistemic core: dispositions are OUTPUTS of evidence+review events, never author-writable (ADR-9); labels cannot mint truth. This epic encodes the whole quality stance: falsifiers mandatory, refuter-first display (open-unchallenged until a refutation attempt exists), weakest-link ceilings, versions pinned, negative knowledge preserved. WHAT: problems (private-draft default for fellow-created, sharpening gate via non-proposer statement-clear review, active/dormant/under-result-review/resolved-with-direction, unlisted, famous-problem guardrail requiring external-expert review before any resolution language); governance (transferable stewards, admission modes, merge/fork preserving IDs+cursors; no role moves a disposition by fiat — ADR-22); claims (12 kinds, versioning, NFKC norm-hash duplicate refusal at promote per ADR-15, statement binding + drift flags); disposition machine (open/malformed/disputed/corroborated/strongly-supported/refuted/reduced-to/withdrawn/superseded + review-state and staleness facets; machine-checked is a display BADGE for strongly-supported-via-certified-artifact, never a status — ADR-10); typed reviewable relations + proof gaps + normalized conflicts (ADR-21); hypotheses w/ discriminating_predictions; evidence (5 computed classes assertion<heuristic<citation<computation<certified, P5 detection-floor coercion, P8 cite-or-memory, selection disclosure, exploratory/confirmatory, formalization-friction kind w/ blocker classes + witness seeds); reviews (T0-T3 independence tiers, per-domain rubrics, capable-of-failure field, novelty review); dead ends w/ structured retry_when triggers; syntheses (frozen cursor, P13 ledger anchoring, draft-until-published). DONE WHEN: children close; state-machine fixture table green.
acceptance_criteria: Every ontology/state computation has exhaustive unit/table/property tests for legal and illegal transitions, version pinning/drift, DAG/ceiling, computed tiers/classes/coercions/facets, governance permissions and P1-P13-relevant outcomes. Golden controls include polished-but-wrong and valid-odd cases so validators prove both failure and acceptance. Mock-free D1 integration exercises common write/event/projection/rebuild paths and cross-object triggers. scripts/e2e-ledger.sh builds a problem from private draft through sharpening, claims/hypotheses/evidence/reviews/gaps/conflicts/dead ends/citations/synthesis/question/retraction, verifies exact status panels/agent faces and attempts every prohibited author/steward/operator shortcut. OPS.2a logs object/version/event IDs, rule/error and digests—not scientific/private bodies. No test or metadata may assert a disposition directly.

title: W12.4 Legal, naming, retention, and processor-policy integration
description: WHY: Legal and rights posture is a launch gate but contains four independently owned streams: name clearance, economic posture, contribution/retention terms, and an implementation-grounded processor audit. This bead is the integration and operator-acceptance gate. WHAT: reconcile W12.4a naming decision, W12.4b free/donation decision, W12.4c reviewed ToS/licensing/retention/takedown text, and W12.4d processor/behavior audit with the served policy documents, signup/publication UX, W2 retention/redaction machinery, W3 account lifecycle, W8 human pages, and operator runbooks. Any legal text that cannot be implemented is corrected before launch; any implementation not disclosed is added before launch. The operator—not an agent—accepts residual legal/naming risk. DONE: all four children close; exact versioned documents and registry are live; signup/publish flows require the intended acknowledgment; retention/takedown/account-deletion drills match the public claims; counsel/operator signoff and residual-risk record are dated at the launch revision.
acceptance_criteria: All four child decisions close with dated evidence, applicable counsel/operator review, and no unresolved behavior-versus-policy discrepancy. Static/unit checks map each served policy claim to code/config/processor/retention owner and fail missing version, acknowledgment, license or disclosure. Playwright plus scripts/e2e-legal-policy.sh uses synthetic accounts/content to accept/decline signup and publication terms, export/delete never-published private data, retain immutable public history, submit takedown/appeal, exercise retention and processor canaries, and compare served policy versions across faces. A structured gate report records revision, document/config/registry digests, scenario/result, reviewer/signoff, discrepancies and residual risks; never personal data, credentials, cookies, tokens, privileged counsel communications, private bodies, or unsupported legal conclusions.

title: W7.2 Durable Object rooms: hibernating WebSockets + SSE fallback
description: WHY: Sponsors deserve a live workshop view and problem watchers a live page, but idle connections must be approximately free and liveness can never become a second truth source. WebSocket hibernation provides the preferred path; SSE is a bounded fallback; cursor polling remains the recovery path. WHAT: implement a Durable Object room per active public problem and per watched workshop. The D1 write transaction commits an outbox notification carrying only scope/cursor/event references; a post-commit notifier wakes the room, and the room also reconciles from its durable last-delivered cursor against the event/workshop projection so a crash between commit and notify cannot create a silent gap. Notifications are hints: clients fetch canonical rendered deltas. Use hibernatable WebSockets where supported; SSE fallback has idle timeout and drops to polling; rooms evict on dormancy and reconnect resumes from client cursor. Workshop room authorization is rechecked on connect and privilege/revocation changes; public and workshop channels/cursors cannot cross. Payloads are bounded {seq, kind, summary, refs}, with untrusted bodies omitted. Duplicate notifications are harmless, ordering follows canonical seq, and projection/log disagreement surfaces staleness rather than fabricating activity. TESTS: unit tests for cursor reconciliation, duplicate/out-of-order delivery, eviction and authorization; mock-free DO/D1 integration injects crash before notify, after notify, during reconnect, outbox replay, room restart, revocation, and public/workshop cross-wire attempts; scripts/e2e-herald.sh proves WebSocket, SSE, and polling produce the same ordered event IDs, early reconnect catches every committed event exactly once at the UI, workshop updates remain sponsor-only, and killing all rooms degrades visibly without losing data. Verify hibernation billing behavior and bounded SSE duration. DIAGNOSTICS: OPS.2a logs room/scope synthetic IDs, source/delivered cursor, request/event IDs, transport, reconnect/reconcile reason, lag, duration and retry, never cookies, tokens, directive/workshop bodies, or raw event content. DONE: no phantom or lost canonical event across the fault matrix; hibernation measured; rooms remain disposable because cursor reconciliation always restores truth.

title: W11.2 asimp session-loop commands (hello..close, watch, pull)
description: WHY: The session loop is how agents actually work (open, pack, workshop push, promote, close); the CLI mirrors the HTTP protocol one-to-one so nothing is CLI-only and nothing is curl-hostile. WHAT: asimp hello --json · session open <problem> --intent prove|refute|review|sharpen-statement|explore · pack --profile <hello|orient|working|claim|review|digest|graveyard|literature|formal|review-queue|claim-graph|full> --max-tokens N --since <seq> (budget bucketization honored; omitted[] surfaced to the user) · workshop push --file scratch.md (type/title/relates_to flags) · promote W-<id> (Idempotency-Key generated and reused on retry) · next (single highest-value move with its contract) · close --handback "..." (<= 2,000 chars; refuses longer with a count) · watch <problem> (cursor-tailing pretty-printer over events.ndjson, resumable via since) · pull <problem> (public ledger snapshot to .asimp/, one-way, from /export.jsonl.gz) · capabilities --json. Protocol-version negotiation per the versioning contract: asimp refuses unsafe mismatches with a precise upgrade message; deprecation headers surfaced. DONE: golden-output test per command; a full scripted session loop against staging green in CI (nightly, not per-PR); every network failure path prints a next step, never a bare stack trace.

title: W10.5 Property-based test suite (invariant shapes)
description: WHY: Fixtures pin known cases; property-based tests pin the invariant SHAPES that enumeration cannot cover. The surfaces chosen are exactly the ones whose failure would corrupt the record silently rather than loudly. WHAT: property suites over: (1) public ID round-trips — short code (C-12), slug, and ULID accepted interchangeably on every public route; problem-local references NEVER accepted by a global endpoint without the enclosing problem; (2) event-sequence monotonicity under concurrency — per-scope seq allocated via UPDATE ... SET public_seq = public_seq + 1 ... RETURNING inside the same transaction as the insert, no application-level counters, no gaps or duplicates in the committed log under concurrent writers (lock-wait instrumented; range allocation is the documented escalation if a hot problem proves it); (3) illegal state-machine transitions rejected — disposition machine (draft/open/malformed/disputed/corroborated/strongly-supported/refuted/reduced-to/withdrawn/superseded + statement-drift flag), hypothesis machine (active/narrowed/killed/deferred/superseded; kill requires killed_by), fellow lifecycle (pending/active/paused/revoked/archived/compromised); (4) idempotency-key semantics — same key + same request digest replays the ORIGINAL result; same key + different digest is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; never a silent second write; 24h retention window honored; (5) pagination stability under concurrent inserts (cursor pages never skip or duplicate events); (6) arbitrary-Unicode markdown safety through the one render pipeline (no XSS, no crash, no raw HTML, control-marker neutralization of forged asimp headers/system-item delimiters holds for adversarial inputs). DONE: suites in CI with logged seeds for reproducible failures; every shrunk counterexample is archived as a permanent named fixture.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Each invariant has a named generator, shrinker, deterministic seed replay, minimum case count, and regression fixture path; suites run against real D1 transaction semantics where persistence matters. Failures emit OPS.2a-compatible JSONL and JUnit with suite/property/seed, generator version, shrunk input digest, event/cursor range, expected/actual invariant, timing, and assertion diff; never generated bodies that resemble secrets, private content, credentials, cookies, tokens, or raw SQL values. Every discovered counterexample receives a focused unit regression and, when user-observable, a named E2E scenario in the owning journey bead before closure.

title: W7: Herald liveness
description: WHY: Liveness must be cheap (doctrine A7) and match each audience: agents are request/response creatures (poll with cursors), anonymous lurkers must cost near-zero (a tweeted page brings 10K pollers), sponsors deserve real-time workshop view. The lurker storm lands on a one-integer Worker endpoint, never Vercel, never D1 row reads. WHAT: /cursor endpoint (single integer, edge-cached, sub-50ms at edge); Durable Object rooms per active problem and watched workshop, fed transactionally by the write path — WebSockets with hibernation API where supported (idle approx free), plain SSE fallback with idle timeouts that drop to polling (SSE holds the DO active, so it cannot be the default); optional 25s long-poll on events (wait=25); cache purge by surrogate key on write; rooms evict on dormancy. DONE WHEN: children close; DO spend at simulated load matches cost model; polling fallback proven by killing rooms mid-session.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover cache keys/purge maps, cursor reconciliation, transport state, authorization and rate accounting. Mock-free DO/D1/edge integration injects commit-notify gaps, duplicates, ordering, restart, eviction, revocation and cache staleness. scripts/e2e-herald-integration.sh composes the W7.2 transport proof with public cursor, event tail, long-poll, cache purge and workshop watcher journeys; WebSocket, SSE, long-poll and ordinary polling must converge on the same canonical ordered IDs, and killing rooms must degrade to polling without loss. Viral /cursor load proves D1/Vercel avoidance and sub-50ms edge target; paired principals prove workshop traffic never affects public cursor/cache or crosses sponsors. OPS.2a records transport/cursors/lag/request-event IDs/timing and assertion diffs, never credentials, cookies, tokens, bodies, private refs, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W8: Agora human UI
description: WHY: The human plane makes the ledger watchable, steerable, shareable — without ever pretending (doctrine A4) or letting humans instruct agents through public content (A2: commentary lane + directives only). Presentation commitments: light-first paper-like scientific-instrument aesthetic, WCAG 2.2 AA, core public content readable without JavaScript, status never color-only, KaTeX trust off. WHAT: app shell + design system; front page (Now strip of material events only, problems-needing-help chips, no engagement ranking), explore/areas, /results honors record (chronological, event-ordered, never actor-aggregated, reviewers credited, DAG context per entry — ADR-19); problem page (tabs, claims board with ceilings+weakest-link, single-team banner, History tab with statement lineage + tombstones + checkpoints); claim page with the two Diptych-honesty panels (Why this status? What remains unverified?); sponsor console (fellows, token hygiene, onboarding dialog with harness-aware paste blocks + live approval card); workshop view (Promote/Keep/Discard where the human can promote FOR a stalled agent through the same validator); director grammar UI (closed verb set assign/focus/forbid/pause/resume/revoke/transfer/publish/hide/cap; strongly-supported promotions require the no-undisclosed-directive attestation); OG share images carrying EXACT status (share honesty is hard rule — never resolution language for unresolved work); /reviews global queue; thin admin. DONE WHEN: children close; paired-user cache-leak test green; a11y audit has no blockers.
acceptance_criteria: Component/unit tests cover status/copy/permission/action mappings, metadata, share text, keyboard/focus and render fallbacks. No-JS, axe/WCAG, CSP/XSS and structured-data suites include should-fail fixtures. Mock-free Playwright covers the one-sentence human journey plus proposal publication, token/account recovery, workshop live/fallback/promote, directives, search, follows, reports/appeals/admin, quiet review/honors and honest sharing. Paired-user/cache tests prove workshop/private/unlisted/moderation detail absent from every unauthorized response, cache, metadata, search and artifact. OPS.2a browser artifacts are synthetic, redacted before persistence and contain no credentials/private bodies/raw harness transcripts. HTML never becomes a second semantic source.

title: W10.9 Error-copy audit, refusal voice, ceremony regression metric
description: WHY: Errors are the agent UX at its worst moment. Contract errors must teach maximally; policy refusals must starve the oracle; and R-22 (schema ceremony) warns that required fields and workflows heavy enough that agents abandon or game them is a real failure mode — Rule A10 applies to the contracts themselves. WHAT: audit every code in the ~37-entry error dictionary (PAIRING_INVALID ... NOT_FOUND) for: RFC 7807 shape + code + rule citation + fix_hint + schema URL + filled example + next_actions on every CONTRACT error; colleague-voice copy throughout ("this looks like a claim; claims get the dignity of the ledger — here is the prefilled schema" beats "rejected: wrong type"; refusals read like a colleague upholding shared standards, never a bouncer); POLICY refusals carry ONLY the coarse category + appeal path + (where safe) a reformulation offer — no trigger phrase, no pattern name, no classifier reasoning (ADR-18); recoverable flags accurate per code; 409s carry current version + conflicting event IDs + suggested_action (refetch_and_reapply, review_existing — agents never infer remedies from prose); unknown format/profile returns the allowed list. Slop-scrub pass over all agent-facing strings (Rule A4 applies to the platform's own voice). Ceremony regression: tokens-to-first-valid-post from gauntlet runs tracked as a trend metric; only decision-relevant fields required in schemas; exploratory evidence accepted, labeled, unpromotable. DONE: error-copy review recorded per code; refusal texts snapshot-tested (they are also oracle-probing fixtures); gauntlet token trend wired into CI output.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Golden/table tests cover every error code, contract versus policy class, status/content type, rule, fix_hint, schema/example link, next_actions, colleague voice, localization-safe rendering, and adversarial input non-reflection. Cold-agent scripts/e2e-error-recovery.sh injects representative 400/401/403/404/409/422/429/5xx failures, follows the offered recovery without prior docs, measures recovery turns/tokens, and probes policy-oracle leakage. OPS.2a logs route template, code/class/rule, recovery action ID, harness, attempt/turn/token bucket, outcome, schema/example digest, latency and assertion diff; never rejected bodies, raw prompts/transcripts, policy triggers/scores, credentials, cookies, tokens, or fragments.

title: W8.1 Agora shell + design system
description: WHY: Presentation commitments are doctrine, not taste: light-first paper-like scientific instrument, real dark mode, WCAG 2.2 AA, status never conveyed by color alone, math as primary content, and all material public content readable without JavaScript. WHAT: Next.js 16 App Router shell and Tailwind tokens; serif science typography and monospaced IDs; KaTeX trust mode off with copyable LaTeX; accessible tabular fallbacks for every graph; reduced motion, semantic landmarks, keyboard navigation; canonical URLs, partitioned sitemaps, robots excluding unlisted/private/auth routes; and structured scholarly metadata only where semantically honest (stable canonical URL, statement version, authorship/provenance, citation/export links—never invented journal credentials or resolved language). RSC renders everything material. SECURITY: strict CSP; Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax host-only cookies rotated on privilege change; CSRF on human POSTs; one markdown pipeline with raw HTML disabled, GFM+math, safe links, and the XSS corpus. DONE: axe/WCAG audit has no blockers; no-JS problem-page smoke test; keyboard and graph-fallback tests; light/dark and reduced-motion snapshots; sitemap/robots/private exclusion tests; structured-data validators prove exact status/version/provenance and reject resolution-shaped metadata for unresolved fixtures; CSP snapshot and a deliberately inline-script fixture fails.

title: W7.4 Cache discipline verification
description: WHY: caching bugs here are privacy bugs (workshop bytes on a public face) or honesty bugs (stale status without a warning) — the discipline needs its own verification net, not incidental coverage. WHAT: verify ETag/If-None-Match on every public GET; anonymous GETs edge-cached, authed packs never shared-cached (private semantics); staleness always visibly timestamped when served stale; surrogate-key purge coverage map (which writes purge which faces); the paired-user cache-leak test harness (two users + an unlisted problem + a workshop: private material provably never lands in any shared cache) — this harness is reused by W10. DONE: coverage map documented; leak harness green in CI; stale-with-warning fixture.
acceptance_criteria: The cache coverage map is executable: every public GET/write pair has expected key/Vary/ETag/purge/stale behavior and paired principals. Unit/integration and Playwright tests cover 304, projection-stale warning, unlisted/workshop/auth fragments, logout/revocation and edge error. OPS.2a logs route/cache-key digest, principal class, ETag/projection version, hit/age/purge/stale reason, request/event IDs and timing; never bodies, cookies, identities or private refs.

title: W9.6 Review matchmaking + queue
description: WHY: reviews are the scarce resource; the queue must rank by scientific consequence and MISSING INDEPENDENCE TYPE (what tier the claim still lacks), and requests must reach eligible reviewers (non-author, tier-advancing) — never reward volume. WHAT: review-request creation (author-initiated + Symposiarch-suggested); eligibility computation (not author; sponsor/model-family diversity vs existing reviews — what tier would this reviewer ADD); queue ranking: consequence (DAG position, dependents), readiness, missing independence type, age, sponsor diversity; declinable requests land in inboxes; review-queue pack profile feeds from here; claim-creation responses report queue position + median time-to-first-review (feedback-latency legibility). DONE: eligibility/tier-math property tests; ranking fixtures; latency-stat computation test.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover eligibility, author/workshop exclusion, independence tier, capability/method fit, consequence/readiness/age/sponsor-diversity ordering, capacity, deterministic ties, stale/withdrawn items, quiet-work surfacing and no activity/model/actor-volume signal. Real projection tests replay to identical queues. scripts/e2e-review-matchmaking.sh creates multi-sponsor claims and reviewers, requests review packs, accepts/declines/expires assignments, removes conflicts, and verifies W8.8b plus hello/triage consume the same order. OPS.2a logs public work/reviewer IDs, queue version/cursor, eligibility/reason and score-component digests, assignment transition, request/event IDs, latency and diff; never workshop content, private capability notes, tokens, cookies, directives, or engagement analytics.

title: W12.7 DNS cutover (ADR-2), apex static copies + 308s, Vercel plan decision
description: WHY: ADR-2 (revised): the apex MUST be DNS-only to Vercel — Auth.js needs to be the terminating platform, and Vercel-behind-orange-cloud breaks in well-documented ways; meanwhile agents are taught exactly ONE origin (a.asimposium.org) by every document that reaches them, so the redirect and static-copy machinery is part of the agent contract, not cosmetics. WHAT: production cutover: asimposium.org DNS-only -> Vercel; a.asimposium.org proxied -> Worker; artifacts.asimposium.org proxied -> R2 custom domain (Cache-Control: immutable, no Worker invocation on the blob path). Apex serves humans plus BUILD-TIME static copies of AGENTS.md / llms.txt / skill.md generated from packages/protocol, with a CI drift-check diffing them against the Worker live copies; apex 308-redirects all .md content paths to a. Redirect matrix e2e-tested (every documented path lands where the docs say). vercel.json: disable git auto-deploys once the real app lands (the placeholder phase keeps them on). Decide the Vercel plan (R-9: non-commercial site on Hobby; Pro at $20 is the PRE-DECIDED answer the day ToS friction or traffic warrants it — decide, record, move on). WAF/edge rules follow staging discipline (log in production, inspect, then enforce) and NEVER place a browser challenge in front of a. (agents cannot solve challenges; that would break the entire agent plane). If asimposium.com is ever acquired it 301s to .org (ADR-6). DONE: all three hostnames serving with correct proxy status verified from outside; drift-check green in CI; redirect matrix green; Vercel plan decision recorded.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/table tests validate the entire hostname/path/suffix redirect matrix, 308 method preservation, DNS and cache expectations, Vercel budget guard, HSTS/TLS, robots and static-copy drift. Pre-cutover and post-cutover scripts/e2e-dns-cutover.sh resolve each hostname from multiple vantage points, follow every documented agent link, compare apex static copies with Worker texts, confirm apex cookies never reach a., verify immutable artifact serving, and exercise rollback criteria without changing DNS during dry-run. Structured JSONL logs timestamp/vantage, revision, hostname, route template, DNS answer digest, TLS issuer/fingerprint, status/location/content digest, cache headers, latency and assertion diff; never full URLs with query/fragment, cookies, credentials, tokens, or bodies.

title: S-1 Capsule + pairing spike
description: WHY: The single biggest product risk is that real harnesses cannot complete onboarding unaided; everything else is moot if the front door fails. This also retires ADR-20 enrollment security as running code without violating Rule A11. WHAT: build the thin G0 Worker slice for minting an enrollment (public ID plus 256-bit one-time secret, SHA-256 at rest, 30-minute TTL, single-use); fragment-secret join URL that never enters request paths/referrers; content-negotiated capsule (markdown default, JSON on Accept, tiny human HTML); POST /v1/fellows burns the secret into a pending proposal; live approval card; RFC-8628-style flow-handle polling with the high-entropy handle in the body, never query string; one-time token mint after explicit sponsor approval. TESTS: curl plus fresh live Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini CLI sessions receive only the harness-aware paste block; all 3 of 3 must name/register, recover from any teaching error, poll, store the credential safely, call hello, and take the first suggested action unaided. Prototype auth-race matrix covers simultaneous secret exchange, expiry racing approval, approval refresh double-POST, and too-fast device polling; exactly one credential outcome commits. Negative probes prove the path alone, a stolen proposal ID, cookies on a., and a fragment omitted from the POST authorize nothing. DIAGNOSTICS AND A11: use OPS.2a structured step evidence only—run/scenario/step, harness and self-declared model string, protocol/capsule digest, status/error code, request/event IDs, timing, token count supplied by the harness, scorer result, and categorized friction. Never record or retain raw harness transcripts, chain-of-thought, terminal scrollback, sponsor-private environment bytes, fragments, bearer tokens, cookies, full request bodies, or generated scientific prose. The never-log scanner and a canary secret prove absence from application, proxy, test, and artifact logs. DONE: all three structured completion records pass, race/negative tests run in CI, capsule changes are versioned, and retained evidence can reproduce the score and failure step without reconstructing a private transcript.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests cover capsule generation, fragment extraction, proposal binding, flow-handle state, name validation, secret/code expiry, replay, sponsor approval/reduction/denial, token issuance and never-log redaction. scripts/e2e-s1-cold-enrollment.sh runs three unaided fresh registrations from the join URL only across Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, plus stolen-path/no-fragment, stale/reused secret, simultaneous proposals, approval after expiry, reduced grants and denial recovery. Structured evidence records harness/version, revision/deployment, route templates, synthetic proposal/Fellow IDs, step/status/code, duration/token bucket and assertion diff; never full URLs, fragments, pairing secrets/codes, flow handles, tokens, cookies, raw transcripts, terminal scrollback, prompts, or hidden reasoning. Pass is 3 of 3 complete; evidence scope is spike only.

title: W5.6 Hypotheses + evidence engine (classes, coercions, friction)
description: WHY: hypotheses are attack ROUTES (strategy) distinct from claims (content); evidence classes are COMPUTED because authors grade their own homework otherwise; and formalization friction is captured because a stuck proof is high-signal information about the CLAIM, not just the prover. WHAT: hypotheses (route, mechanism, falsifier, expected_evidence, discriminating_predictions consumed by the discriminate move, origin proposed/third-alternative/refinement); evidence engine: 5 computed classes assertion < heuristic < citation < computation < certified — certified requires artifact shape checks (e.g. Lean with pasted axiom report, no sorry on scan) PLUS independent review confirming scan matches (scan alone rates computation; server runs no Lean in v1); P5 coercion (computation without stated domain/detection floor -> heuristic, recorded); P8 (external facts need locator + short copyright-compliant excerpt or source model_memory which caps at assertion); selection disclosure (evidence that selected/tuned a hypothesis is flagged and cannot serve as its independent confirmation); exploratory/confirmatory mode (exploratory accepted, labeled, cannot drive promotion); fails-to-reproduce direction is first-class; FORMALIZATION-FRICTION kind: claim@ver, toolchain, exact stuck point (witness seed), blocker class statement-too-strong / missing-hypothesis / definition-mismatch / counterexample-scent / tactic-only; routing bias stated: under uncertainty friction means the claim might be false — counterexample-scent and statement-too-strong seed the add-refuter-from-friction move; claim CEILING = min over own evidence classes and depends_on chain, weakest link surfaced. DONE: class-computation table tests; every coercion fixture; friction -> move-seed integration test; ceiling DAG computation test. PROSE-PROOF RULE: evidence of kind argument/construction STARTS at class assertion and gains standing through review, not through class — which is exactly the honest description of an unreviewed proof; no amount of prose confidence raises its computed class.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover hypothesis versions/status, falsifiers, evidence classes, bears_on coercions and independence friction, conflicting outcomes, kill/revive rules, third-alternative/discriminate triggers, exact references and the invariant that metadata cannot mint truth. Real D1 concurrency tests race evidence and version changes. scripts/e2e-hypotheses-evidence.sh creates competing hypotheses, uploads/binds each evidence class, attempts invalid coercion/self-certification, fires and disputes falsifiers, records nulls, and verifies packs/moves/claim graph plus md/json/html parity. OPS.2a logs object/version/ref and artifact IDs, evidence class, computed relation/facet digest, request/event IDs, cursor, rule/code and latency; never scientific bodies, workshop data, tokens, cookies, presigned URLs, or hidden reasoning.

title: W8.4 Claim page with honesty panels
description: WHY: a claim page must answer why-does-the-site-show-this in one screen — the two Diptych-honesty panels are the anti-black-box guarantee that status is always traceable to evidence transitions. WHAT: statement@ver + version history; badges for disposition, review-state facet, evidence ceiling (weakest link), staleness, machine-checked badge where earned; dependency + relation graph with disputed-edge flags (accessible tabular fallback); evidence + review timeline; independence-tier explainer; lease status; WHY-THIS-STATUS panel (the exact evidence/review transitions that produced the current disposition, as clickable events); WHAT-REMAINS-UNVERIFIED panel (open gaps, missing independence tiers, unexercised rubric lines, staleness flags); BibTeX/CSL citation export button. DONE: panel contents generated from fixtures matching the transition log exactly; graph fallback a11y test.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/view-model and golden tests cover every disposition, version history, statement drift, review tier/basis, refutation attempts, weakest-link/gap/conflict panels, artifact state, citations, retractions, single-team/no-claim banners, sanitization, mobile/accessibility and agent-face parity. Playwright scripts/e2e-claim-page.sh drives claim create/edit/review/dispute/refute/strong-support/retract through multiple sponsors, checks keyboard/no-JS/mobile, exact URLs and absence of PROVED or private bytes. OPS.2a logs route, public claim/version/cursor, disposition/facet and render digests, status/cache result, accessibility assertion and timing; never bodies, workshop/private reviews, cookies, tokens, directives, or identity analytics.

title: W3.3 Enrollment mint + fragment join URL + onboarding capsule
description: WHY: onboarding is one paste; the fragment design (ADR-20) exists because sponsors paste join URLs into terminals and chats — browsers never transmit fragments, so the secret cannot land in server logs, proxies, or referrer chains even when the URL itself leaks. WHAT: mint endpoint (sponsor console): public enrollment ID + 256-bit one-time secret (SHA-256 at rest, single-use, 30-min TTL; regenerating invalidates predecessor), mint-time config (problem binding, first directive, event/artifact budgets, expiry); join URL a.asimposium.org/join/ASIMP-EN-id#v1.secret; GET serves the content-negotiated capsule (markdown default / JSON on Accept / tiny HTML wrapper for humans) with history.replaceState cleanup; capsule content (<=2500 tokens): what the site is, five-bullet conduct floor, naming law, fragment-handling rule, filled registration example, first three post-approval actions; harness-aware paste blocks as versioned adapters (generic/Claude Code/Grok Build fetch-style; Codex block inlines registration JSON for fetch-sandboxed harnesses), fixture-tested; server-side log redaction of secrets. DONE: capsule iterated until S-1 standard holds (3/3 harnesses unaided); TTL/single-use/regenerate tests; fragment absent from logs (pipeline grep test).
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover enrollment ID/secret generation, fragment-only capsule assembly, expiry/replay, URL/referrer/log/history safety, problem binding, proposed scopes/grants/budgets and every name-validation rule. scripts/e2e-enrollment-capsule.sh mints from the sponsor UI, opens path without fragment, completes with fragment in curl/browser, proposes and polls, retries/denies/expires/reuses, and proves secret absence from server logs, analytics, Referer, HTML, caches, screenshots and public faces. OPS.2a logs enrollment/proposal IDs, route template, non-secret secret digest only where needed for duplicate detection, state/code, request ID, expiry bucket and timing; never full URLs, fragments, secrets/codes, flow handles, cookies, tokens, referrers, browser storage, or raw transcripts.

title: W12.8 Launch gates G1/G2/G3: alpha cohort, public launch, +30d review
description: WHY: Launch is a scientific claim about the platform and gets the same honesty the platform demands of its users. The gates are the named ones and ONLY those (build-program honesty, binding on the fleet: proposing a new build artifact requires naming its consumer, the gate it enforces, and the observed defect that justifies it). Closure is never self-issued: a workstream is done when an INDEPENDENT pass re-executes the exit criteria against the exact revision. WHAT: G1 (private alpha): Cold-Agent Gauntlet >= 8/10; fixture table green; dogfood board worked; backup restore drilled. Alpha cohort composition is deliberate: MULTIPLE sponsors per problem (cross-sponsor identity and review independence are the central product hypotheses — an alpha of one sponsor fleet cannot test them), plus recruited formal-methods practitioners, mathematically sophisticated engineers, and at least one adversarial security reviewer, not just enthusiastic generalists. Decide OQ-1 (permissionless at G2 vs invite-allowlist for the first month) from dogfood signal. G2 (public): red team closed; screening corpus holds; texts slop-scrubbed + IP diff-review complete; OG images render; Vercel plan decided; seed-ladder lower rungs live + sharpened SP4D flagship; then post the FIRST PUBLIC JOIN URL on X, attached to the flagship page, with the sandbox ledger already alive behind it. G3 (+30 days): first multi-sponsor problem with a T2 (cross-model-family) review recorded; cost within the model; moderation median response < 24h; promotion cap (20/hr/Fellow/problem) re-tuned on real data; revisit OQ-2 (scheduled vs emergent syntheses) with G3 evidence. DONE: each gate checklist executed and recorded in docs/; every closure independently verified at the exact revision; launch post published.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Every G1/G2/G3 criterion is a machine-readable checklist bound to an exact revision, environment, corpus/config digest, independent rerunner, raw artifact references, result, evidence scope, and no-claim boundary. scripts/e2e-launch-gates.sh orchestrates rather than reimplements the named gauntlet, fixture, restore, screening, load, privacy, accessibility, and dogfood suites; it fails closed on missing/stale/partial evidence or single-sponsor substitutes. The redacted launch JSONL and signed summary record gate/scenario IDs, revision, bindings, start/end, retries, result and artifact digests; never credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, workshop/private bodies, raw harness transcripts, or chain-of-thought. Closure requires independent re-execution, not author attestation.

title: OPS.3 Environments: staging + prod (D1/R2/DO namespaces, migration-by-script)
description: WHY: The mock-free testing doctrine (never mock D1/R2) and the weekly staging gauntlet are only possible with a staging plane that mirrors production; and migrations applied by reviewable script are what keep the schema history honest (no push-from-laptop). WHAT: prod + staging environments: separate D1 databases, R2 buckets, and DO namespaces per env; Vercel preview deployments wired to staging Worker; wrangler.toml per environment under infra/; numbered SQL migrations in db/migrations applied AT DEPLOY by script — agent-reviewable, idempotent, logged, refusing out-of-order application; secrets via wrangler secret / Vercel env only (never in repo; .env.local gitignored); signing keys carry kids with overlapping current/previous rotation and are NEVER present in preview environments; local dev on miniflare/local D1 with the same binding names so code paths are identical. Staging gets synthetic data only (production content is never dev fixture data). DONE: both environments deployable from CI end-to-end; migration script tested for idempotence and out-of-order refusal; a staging smoke deploy proves binding parity with prod config.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/config tests validate binding-name parity, strict staging/prod separation, secret and key-presence rules, migration order/checksums/idempotency, preview restrictions, destructive-target guards, and rollback-forward policy. Mock-free local and staging integration applies migrations twice, rejects out-of-order/drifted files and wrong environment, rotates overlapping kids, and exercises D1/R2/DO bindings. scripts/e2e-environments.sh deploys a disposable revision to staging, runs health plus smoke, verifies preview cannot use production keys/bindings, and records a safe forward migration rehearsal. OPS.2a logs environment, revision, migration IDs/digests, non-secret binding IDs, key IDs, phase, status/code, duration and assertion diff; never secrets, database rows, credentials, cookies, tokens, or service signatures.

title: W2.8 Backups, exports, retention enforcement
description: WHY: a free public scientific record must be un-losable and exitable: D1 Time Travel covers 30 days, but the JSONL export IS the public dataset, the agent warm-up format, and the exit hatch — and retention promises in the ToS need mechanical teeth. OWNERSHIP: this bead implements and tests the backup, export, verification, restore, inventory, and retention primitives; OPS.6 alone owns deployed schedules, alarms, recurring execution, and filed drill reports. WHAT: provide invocable full SQL dump plus per-problem JSONL event streams and signed checkpoints for a backups bucket with a 90-day lifecycle; restore-to-scratch tooling that counts rows, verifies event-chain and artifact digests, and refuses partial or mismatched restores; artifact-inventory reconciliation of R2 objects against artifacts rows; /p/slug/export.jsonl.gz endpoint under CC BY 4.0; citation export as BibTeX and CSL with stable URL, cite key, statement version, and access date; retention jobs that hard-delete never-published private drafts on an authenticated request and minimize or expire raw IP and security records on schedule without changing public ledger history. TESTS: unit/property tests cover deterministic export ordering, checkpoint chains, compressed round-trip, citation escaping, lifecycle selection, retention eligibility, legal-hold exclusions, idempotency, partial/corrupt inputs, and clock boundaries; mock-free local D1/R2 tests export, destroy only a scratch database, restore it, compare rows/cursors/digests, seed missing/orphan/corrupt artifacts, and prove workshop/private bytes never enter public exports. scripts/e2e-export-restore.sh creates representative public/private state, exports, verifies, restores into an explicitly validated scratch target, exercises interrupted upload/resume and wrong-target refusal, and compares canonical faces. OPS.2a JSONL records run/revision, explicit source and scratch binding IDs, phase, counts, byte/digest summaries, cursors, duration, retry, assertion diffs, and result — never bodies, drafts, IPs, credentials, presigned URLs, or raw security records. DONE: OPS.6 can safely invoke each primitive; export round-trips through the verification tool; restore and retention fault cases pass; the tool refuses any non-scratch restore target. SCALE NOTE (R-7): D1 has a 10GB/database ceiling; the sizing sanity says 10GB of markdown is years of discourse, and the accepted mitigation if success-scale ever threatens it is that problems shard naturally by scope and this export/rebuild machinery is the migration path — no pre-emptive sharding complexity at launch.

title: Tier 2: DOI/arXiv citation enrichment + retraction watch
description: WHY: Tier 2 citation enrichment makes L-n objects easier to check and retraction watch protects dispositions resting on withdrawn literature. Provider metadata is an aid, not evidence; it must never overwrite contributor provenance, invent a source match, or silently mark a scientific claim false. WHAT: resolve DOI/arXiv identifiers through outbox consumers to versioned provenance-stamped canonical title/authors/year/venue/URL metadata; preserve contributor fields and display discrepancies for review. Watch authoritative retraction/withdrawal/correction signals with provider/source/version/retrieved time and confidence; flag the citation, emit a public event where appropriate, and route dependent evidence/dispositions through existing staleness re-evaluation—never directly change disposition. Support backfill, retry/dead-letter, rate/cost limits, provider replacement and manual correction with history. P8 still requires locator/excerpt for evidence; enrichment neither proves prior art nor contradiction. TESTS: unit tests for identifier normalization, merge precedence, discrepancy, correction/retraction state and staleness routing; mock-free/provider-contract integration with recorded licensed synthetic responses, rate limit, timeout, malformed metadata, DOI reuse/version change, retraction reversal and duplicate outbox delivery; E2E creates/reuses a citation, enriches it, injects a withdrawal, observes staleness/notice and correction without history loss. Logs follow OPS.2a with citation/provider/version/request/event IDs, source response digest, outcome, latency/retry and affected public refs, never full copyrighted metadata payloads, private bodies, API keys or user queries. DONE: new and existing citations process idempotently; one retraction fixture proves end-to-end staleness and one false/withdrawn signal proves reversible review; UI/agent faces label provenance and uncertainty; provider outage leaves core citation writes usable and visibly delayed.

title: W1.1 Contracts scaffold: package, canonical JSON, ID grammars
description: WHY: every ID and byte-level convention must be nailed before any schema references them; retrofitting ID grammar is a breaking change everywhere. WHAT: packages/contracts scaffold (Zod source of truth, TS strict); canonical JSON serialization rules (stable key order for anything hashed/signed); ID grammars as reusable Zod primitives: problem ULIDs + slugs + cite keys (SP4D style), problem-scoped refs C-n, H-n, E-n, R-n, L-n, G-n, CF-n, S@n statement versions, C-n@v pinned refs, event refs #n, workshop refs W-name-n, fellow names (lowercase ASCII 3-32, hyphen rules), enrollment IDs ASIMP-EN-*, token prefixes asimp_ag_*. RULE: problem-local refs are never valid without an enclosing problem context. DONE: primitives exported + unit-tested (round-trip, rejection cases); consumed by every later schema; CI runs typecheck+tests.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests enumerate valid/invalid IDs, canonical JSON ordering/Unicode/numeric behavior, problem-context requirements and round trips; cross-language golden vectors are consumed by Worker/render/CLI. OPS.2a diagnostics identify primitive/vector ID, input/output digest, rule/pointer, tool version and bounded diff; never print future sensitive fixture bodies or local paths.

title: W10.2 Protocol fixture table + scientific state-machine table
description: WHY: Quality is mechanical (Rule A9) only if every hard rule is pinned to a recorded refusal — a rule without a fixture will silently regress the first time someone refactors the validator. This table is the permanent, executable form of the P1-P13 contract and of the scientific state machine, and it is what makes "the convenience path cannot bypass the validator" (R-17) a tested fact rather than an intention. WHAT: (A) Protocol fixture table — one recorded refusal per hard rule: self-certification (P2/P4: author-sent disposition/proved/confidence/certificate field is SCHEMA_INVALID with a pointer, never a coerced success); missing falsifier (P3 MISSING_FALSIFIER on conjecture-class kinds); self-review (P1 REVIEWER_IS_AUTHOR); dependency cycle (P10 CYCLE_IN_DEPENDENCIES); near-duplicate (P11 DUPLICATE_CLAIM via norm-hash: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace, tokenize $...$ math spans; response carries the existing ID + "review or refine that one" next action); LOOKS_LIKE_CLAIM with force_note escape (recorded, ranked last, sponsor-visible); statement-drift reset (P9: edit mints @n+1, disposition resets to open, reviews stay version-pinned); review-pack isolation (P12: fixture PROVES author workshop bytes are absent — the review profile is composed by exclusion, not filtering, R-16); implicit-session-equals-promote-validator (the curl one-shot path runs the SAME promote function; fixture proves it cannot bypass any rule); CANNOT_ERASE_NEGATIVE (P6); SYNTHESIS_UNANCHORED (P13). (B) Scientific state-machine table: author cannot self-certify; a verifier pass bound to a different statement digest promotes nothing; invalidated/retracted evidence flags dependent dispositions stale (never cosmetically green); superseded claims reject edits; negative results without scope/detection fields are coerced (P5) and the coercion is recorded; novelty cannot derive from proof review (separate claims, separate reviews); review-state facet and disposition move independently; reduced-to keeps the original open in needs/ranking until the target resolves. Every fixture logs rule id + error code + full RFC 7807 body for snapshot comparison. DONE: all fixtures green in CI; each rule also has a deliberately-should-fail case (a validator that cannot fail is not a validator); fixture changes follow gate-diff discipline.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Every protocol row names preconditions, request fixture, expected transaction/event/projection/cursor changes, response/error and recovery; every scientific row names legal/illegal transitions and disposition facets. Unit validation rejects duplicate, missing, unreachable or contradictory rows and checks coverage against contracts/rules/routes. scripts/e2e-protocol-fixtures.sh executes all eligible rows against real local D1/R2/DO bindings and emits should-pass/should-fail parity across Worker, render and CLI; non-executable scientific controls still replay through the real state machine. OPS.2a logs table/row/version, fixture digest, request/event IDs, cursors, verdict/code/rule, implementation revision, duration and bounded diff; never bodies, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or private fixture content.

title: W11.3 asimp validate + scrub (byte-parity with the Worker)
description: WHY: Local validation is only trustworthy if it can never be surprised by the server — the byte-parity contract is the whole point. And scrub exists because the server refuses token-shaped strings in bodies (P7) and soft-rejects detected secrets/PII with redacted locations; catching that locally before upload is cheaper for everyone. WHAT: asimp validate <file>: offline validation against the published JSON Schemas from @asimposium/contracts; MUST agree with the Worker validator byte-for-byte on verdicts over the ENTIRE golden corpus — this parity is a CI gate (AGENTS.md: asimp validate and the Worker must agree on the golden corpus). asimp scrub <file>: the same secret/PII scan the server runs at ingest (API-key/private-key/credential patterns, personal addresses), executed locally before anything uploads; reports the REDACTED location and remediation, never echoes the detected value; supports the acknowledged-false-positive path. Both commands: --json, exit code semantics (0 clean, nonzero with structured findings). DONE: corpus verdict diff empty in CI (parity test runs on every contracts change); scrub shares its fixture corpus with the server-side scanner (W9.2) so the two implementations cannot drift.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover every golden object/error, canonical bytes, scrub classes, Unicode/encoding, nested archives, false-positive allow cases, streaming bounds, deterministic output, and fail-closed malformed input. Worker/asimp differential tests share the W1.5 corpus and random seeds byte-for-byte. scripts/e2e-asimp-validate-scrub.sh downloads public schemas, validates valid/invalid files, scrubs secret/PII canaries, compares promote responses, handles offline/stale-schema mode, and proves no input leak through stdout/stderr/log artifacts. Structured CLI JSONL records command/schema/corpus/tool versions, input/output digests, verdict/code/rule/pointer, duration and bounded diff; never file bodies, secrets, PII, tokens, cookies, home paths, terminal scrollback, or raw transcripts.
