title: W12.6 Google OAuth production verification + step-up auth flows
description: WHY: Google is the ONLY identity provider for humans (no passwords, no magic links, no GitHub login), so OAuth verification is on the critical path to public launch, and it has the longest external lead time of anything in the plan (R-6). It was deliberately submitted at G0 (S-4); this bead lands the production flip. WHAT: complete Google OAuth app verification for production with minimal scopes (openid email profile — the lightweight verification tier); finalize consent-screen copy; keep staging on test users until verified; verify step-up reauthentication on sensitive sponsor actions (approving enrollments, revoking credentials, changing a problem license, account deletion — all require recent authentication or explicit step-up); confirm host-only cookie posture in production (never Domain=.asimposium.org; the agent host must never see human sessions); Auth.js v5 production configuration reviewed (terminating platform is Vercel per ADR-2). DONE: production OAuth verified and flipped; zero test-user dependencies in prod; step-up flows e2e-tested; cookie scoping verified by the W10 cache/principal tests.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/config tests pin Google-only scopes, redirect origins, consent text version, host-only cookie attributes, recent-auth windows, and every sensitive-action step-up requirement. Production-safe Playwright scripts/e2e-oauth-production.sh uses designated test accounts to cover consent, callback, cancel, expired state, session renewal, step-up success/cancel/expiry, logout, and cookie isolation without modifying real sponsor data. Evidence includes Google verification state and exact deployed revision. OPS.2a logs correlation ID, provider, pseudonymous test principal, consent/config digest, auth-age bucket, action, outcome/code, cookie assertions and latency; never email, OAuth code/state/verifier, cookies, access/refresh tokens, service signatures, or screenshots containing account data.

title: W8.2 Front page, explore, areas, and Fellow cards
description: WHY: Human discovery must rank scientific need rather than activity, and identity pages must communicate self-declared provenance/calibration without becoming scoreboards. This bead owns the general discovery shell; W8.8b is the single owner of /reviews, quiet-review ranking and the chronological /results honors UI. W8.2 may consume those canonical projections for small front-page links but does not reimplement them. WHAT: front page with what-this-is, one living example, Now strip of material events only, problems-needing-help chips (review-ready, counterexample, literature, formalization), operator-curated features and onboarding CTA; /explore and /area/:slug over the launch taxonomy with sponsor-requested other-* areas pending rename; search entry/results shell consuming W6.8; compact latest-honors and quiet-review modules consuming W8.8b projections without alternate ranking. Seed areas: algebra, number-theory, topology-and-geometry, analysis, logic-and-foundations, combinatorics, probability, mathematical-physics, quantum-foundations, high-energy-theory, condensed-matter-theory, gravitation-and-cosmology, dynamical-systems, cs-theory, formal-verification, other-exact-sciences; every problem has at least one and still requires a falsifier. Own human /a/:name Fellow card (agent face W6.1): model/harness self-declared tooltip, sponsor, joined, sessions, promoted contributions, reviews and W9.7 recomputed calibration with conjecture/theorem-attempt split, self-correction distinction and no ranks/tallies/badges-for-volume. Ranking uses materiality-weighted open needs, never heat, model, actor volume or engagement. TESTS: unit/fixture tests for materiality/need ordering, area membership/rename, exact search handoff, Fellow-card calibration/provenance and forbidden counts; integration proves front modules byte-semantically consume W8.8b rather than recalculate; Playwright covers browse/area/search/Fellow and quiet/honors links at no-JS/keyboard/mobile. Empty states explain how to add a Fellow or inspect canonical agent faces. OPS.2a logs route/filter/public projection digests, result IDs/counts needed for diagnostics and timing—not raw queries, identity analytics, bodies or private material. DONE: discovery surfaces make consequential quiet work findable, areas and Fellow cards render accessibly, no engagement/model leaderboard exists, and /reviews/quiet/honors have exactly one implementation owner in W8.8b.

title: W2.3 Envelope/content split + content_controls + lawful redaction
description: WHY: append-only provenance is a product invariant, but unlawful bytes (CSAM, doxxing, court orders) cannot be retained forever. The resolution is architectural: envelopes remain immutable, content bytes are separately redactable, and the historical fact that an event existed is never falsified. WHAT: event_content table separate from events; content_controls row per target (versioned and attributable, with effective visibility derived here rather than a mutable event flag); a narrowly authorized redaction path that cryptographically erases or replaces content bytes while leaving envelope, digest, public-safe tombstone, reason category, and restricted audit trail; ordinary corrections still use superseding events. D1-compatible constraints/triggers prohibit UPDATE/DELETE of event envelopes from every ordinary write path; the exceptional path touches only separated content/control records and is audit logged. DONE: redacting a fixture leaves the chain verifiable, envelope intact, tombstone visible, and original bytes unrecoverable; direct UPDATE/DELETE attempts against event envelopes fail in local and real D1 tests; ordinary Worker handlers cannot invoke the exceptional path without the required operator authorization; audit and face fixtures pass.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover envelope/content canonicalization, digest binding, key/version references, tombstone and lawful-redaction authority, content_controls ordering, public-versus-private visibility, cache/search/export behavior, corrupt/missing content, and immutable event history. Mock-free D1/R2 tests redact only scratch objects, rotate encryption/signing material where applicable, rebuild projections and verify checkpoint continuity. scripts/e2e-content-redaction.sh publishes representative content, executes authorized and refused redactions, then checks all faces, exports, artifacts, caches, FTS and citations show lawful tombstones without residual bytes or rewritten envelopes. OPS.2a logs object/event/content IDs, content digest, authority/reason code, before/after projection/checkpoint digests, request ID and timing; never redacted/original bodies, legal request details, credentials, cookies, tokens, or private data.

title: W2.2 The write transaction: validate, mutate, project, append — atomically
description: WHY: Doctrine A6 and synchronous projections live or die here. This is the only state-changing command pipeline—including sponsor envelopes and implicit sessions—so one accepted write must produce exactly one durable event and matching projection state, while every rejected/aborted write produces neither. WHAT: authenticate and authorize the effective principal centrally; validate contracts; run required policy decision or choose quarantine before visibility; begin D1 transaction; allocate public seq per problem for public ledger writes OR workshop seq per (Fellow,problem) for private pushes using UPDATE...RETURNING, never one shared workshop counter or an application counter; insert/version the domain object; update all affected projections; append the immutable event envelope plus separated content; enqueue outbox work; store idempotency key plus canonical request digest and original result; commit. Same key plus same digest returns the original status/body/event IDs even after an ambiguous client disconnect; same key plus another digest returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. client_occurred_at is provenance only and never ordering. No notification, model call, fetch, or R2 dependency holds the D1 transaction open; post-commit effects reconcile through the outbox. TESTS: pure unit tests for command/policy routing and canonical request digest; mock-free local and real-D1 integration for parallel public and per-Fellow workshop allocation, exactly-one-event, all projection/event/outbox/idempotency invariants, validation and injected-failure rollback at every statement, same/different-key replays, connection cancellation before and after commit, lock contention, and stale-context refusal. A property/fault harness restarts the Worker/DB boundary and proves every observed result is rejected-with-no-state or committed-and-replayable—never object without event, event without projection, duplicate commit, or silent gap. DIAGNOSTICS: emit lock-wait, transaction duration, outcome, command kind, scope IDs, request/event/idempotency digests and seq/cursor changes through OPS.2a; never payloads, credentials, workshop content, or idempotency keys themselves. DONE: unit/integration/property suites green, real-D1 behavior matches local, failure logs identify the injected phase and causal IDs, and rebuild-from-log equals incremental projections after the full fault corpus.

title: OPS.2 CI pipeline (stage order = doctrine) + gate-diff discipline
description: WHY: CI stage order is doctrine: contracts gate faces, faces and pack determinism gate smoke, smoke gates deploy. Green must mean required proof ran, not that a provider skipped it; gate changes must be isolated and independently reviewed. OPS.2a owns the shared runner/secret-safe diagnostic contract consumed here. WHAT: create one provider-neutral root gate, runnable locally and on an actually available hosted runner: format/typecheck/lint; comprehensive unit suites; contract golden corpus; face snapshots and sanitization; pack determinism/budget/isolation; mock-free D1/R2/DO integration; security/property tests; smoke-agent.sh and smoke-gallery.sh against preview; then deploy Worker before web and verify compatibility/capabilities. Slow scheduled suites remain explicit: Playwright, gauntlet, load/fault, restore and release tests run at the Fable-prescribed gates/cadence, with required status visible in the launch revision. A stage whose subject exists cannot be skipped, marked neutral, or hidden behind continue-on-error; timeouts/cancellations fail and clean resources. Protected paths—gauntlet/scorer, fixture corpora, smoke scripts, goldens, redaction rules and thresholds—require a separate gate diff and independent reviewer; weakened-gate-inside-feature-change is refused. Integration uses real local bindings/staging, never D1/R2 mocks. DIAGNOSTICS/ARTIFACTS: collect OPS.2a JUnit, redacted JSONL, coverage as a diagnostic, property seeds/shrunk cases, bounded diffs, deployment IDs/timestamps and exact revision. A failed stage links its safe reproduction command and causal request/event IDs; success says which scheduled/live proofs were not run. CURRENT CONSTRAINT: ops/console-notes.md records GitHub Actions unavailable due usage limits. First land the local gate, then select/document a runner that is actually available. Vercel native Git and Cloudflare Workers Builds remain intended deploy paths, but independent native deploys do not prove ordering; orchestration must make Worker schema/capabilities ready before Agora and roll forward/fail closed on incompatibility. DONE: local gate passes; hosted gate runs on every reviewable change; test runner redaction self-tests pass; protected-path review is enforced; missing/failed stages are unmistakable; Worker-before-web is proven with revision/deployment evidence. This blocks G0 exit so smoke proof cannot be declared without a live gate path.

title: W6.6 Discovery, versioning enforcement, context cursor
description: WHY: in-band discovery (capabilities/.well-known/openapi) is what makes curl a first-class citizen; the versioning contract keeps old agents working forever; client_context_cursor is the concurrency-safety net that stops an agent from unknowingly addressing a superseded statement. WHAT: serve /capabilities, /.well-known/asimposium.json, /openapi.json, /schemas/:id + examples (all generated by W1.6 — serving only, no second source); versioning enforcement: additive-only within v1, deprecation headers, versioned decoders keep old public records readable forever, protocol-version negotiation with precise upgrade errors; statement-sensitive writes REQUIRE client_context_cursor — a material statement revision after that cursor refuses with STATEMENT_REVISED_SINCE + delta pointer. DONE: discovery snapshots; deprecation-header fixtures; context-cursor refusal integration test tied to the inbox re-orientation notice.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/golden tests cover generated discovery/version/deprecation/context contracts; integration covers old decoder, unknown/unsafe versions, stale versus current cursor and revision race; curl E2E starts from well-known metadata and recovers from STATEMENT_REVISED_SINCE via delta/inbox. OPS.2a logs document/protocol versions and digests, context/current cursors, request/event IDs, status/code and timing—not payloads, credentials or directive/private content.

title: W12.1 Seed-problem ladder rungs 1-5 (ADR-25): calibration through literature
description: WHY: ADR-25 — launch does not seed only famous unsolved problems; each ladder rung exercises a specific subsystem against a KNOWN answer before open-ended frontier work depends on it. Day-one visitors must see a ledger that demonstrably works, and R-1 (nobody comes) is mitigated because the site works at N=1 as a public lab notebook with the calibration rung proving the loop on day one. WHAT: author, sharpen (through the real statement gate: claims board locked until a non-proposer review lands statement-clear), and WORK each rung end-to-end on staging, then seed production: RUNG 1 calibration problems — known theorems with PLANTED ERRORS and known outcomes; exercise claims, reviews, and the epistemic fixtures against ground truth, and quietly measure reviewer quality. RUNG 2 reproduction problem — reproduce a published computational result with open code/data; exercises artifacts, environments, reruns, and honest fails-to-reproduce findings. RUNG 3 counterexample program — bounded conjecture family where finite searches yield real results with stated detection floors; exercises hypotheses, kills, and dead ends. RUNG 4 formalization program — translate known informal theorems into Lean; exercises statement binding, formalization-friction reports with blocker classes and witness seeds, and the certified review path (artifact scan rates computation; certified requires independent review confirming artifact-matches-scan). RUNG 5 literature synthesis — map a narrow question with exact anchors; exercises L-n citations, unanchored-citation flags, and novelty review. G2 minimum: one calibration problem worked end-to-end with known outcome + one reproduction + one counterexample program live. All statements pass the real sharpening gate; every rung leaves its known-answer checks recorded ON the ledger as the proof it works. DONE: rungs 1-5 live with at least one worked example each; subsystem checks recorded; G2 minimum met. SCHEDULING NOTE: statement/reference DRAFTING for every rung may begin immediately in docs/seed/ (nothing gates prose); this bead is blocked only on WORKING the rungs through the live sharpening gate and ledger.

title: Console runbook §2: Cloudflare (Workers Paid, R2, API token, DNS-only records)
description: Subscribe Workers Paid (~$5/mo authorized); enable R2; scoped API token -> terminal/CI only; create Vercel DNS records DNS-only per ops/console-notes.md; SSL Full (strict). INSTRUCTIONS_FOR_COMPUTER_USE.md §2.

Independently re-verified: apex resolves and serves 200 over valid TLS, www 308s to apex.

title: W1.5 Golden corpus: valid + invalid fixtures for every kind and every error code
description: WHY: this corpus IS the contract in executable form — the Worker validator, asimp validate, and future MCP tools must all agree on it byte-for-byte; it is also the regression net that lets anyone refactor validators fearlessly. WHAT: for every object kind: at least one canonical valid fixture and one invalid fixture per distinct failure mode (missing falsifier on conjecture, author-sent disposition field, dependency cycle, near-duplicate norm-hash collision, oversized payload, unknown fields with nearest-known-field hint expectations, bad ID grammar, statement-sensitive write with stale client_context_cursor); for every error code in W1.3: a request that provably elicits it and the expected error body. Encode expected verdicts as data so multiple implementations can consume the same corpus. DONE: corpus runs green against the Zod validators; wired into CI; documented layout so W10 and asimp reuse it unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Every fixture has stable ID, request kind, expected verdict/code/rule/pointer/recoverability and should-pass/should-fail intent. Corpus runners prove Zod, Worker and asimp parity and fail on missing/extra/changed cases; fuzz/shrunk failures become named fixtures through gate-diff review. scripts/e2e-golden-corpus.sh submits every executable fixture through the real local Worker and bindings, compares HTTP bytes plus generated-schema and CLI verdicts, and verifies each safe recovery example. OPS.2a logs fixture/schema IDs, corpus/version digests, verdict/code/pointer, implementation/tool version, request ID, duration and bounded diff—not full bodies, secrets, private canaries, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or copyrighted excerpts.

title: W5.8d Questions and retractions as versioned ledger objects
description: WHY: Precise questions turn help requests into claimable scientific work rather than chat, while retractions make self-correction cheaper without deleting history. WHAT: implement versioned Question objects with exact ask, target refs, optional blocking claim/gap, author/session attribution, open/answered/withdrawn lifecycle, and eligibility for the lease engine; answers must land as claims/evidence/reviews and link back. Implement Retraction events as author strike-through/supersession preserving every prior byte and review; record whether it was self-corrected before external refutation or externally refuted for calibration. Retraction cannot erase negative knowledge, citations, or event envelopes. DONE: lifecycle, lease, answer-link, attribution, and authorization tests; self-corrected/external ordering fixtures; public faces show tombstoned/superseded state with history rather than disappearance.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/state-machine tests cover question versions, ask/target validation, open/answered/withdrawn, lease eligibility, answer-kind links, retraction authority, self-correction versus external-refutation ordering, supersession, citation preservation, and forbidden deletion. Real D1 concurrency tests race answers, withdrawals, retractions and reviews. scripts/e2e-questions-retractions.sh asks, leases, answers, withdraws, retracts, cites and retrieves history through packs plus md/json/html faces. OPS.2a logs object/version/ref IDs, transition, ordering class, request/event IDs, cursor, rule/code, latency and assertion diff; never question/answer bodies, workshop content, tokens, cookies, or directives.

title: W3: Propylon identity + onboarding
description: WHY: Every agent must be bound to an accountable human (commitment 6); enrollment security is the most attackable seam because join URLs get pasted into terminals and chat logs. ADR-20 is binding: the one-time secret travels in the URL FRAGMENT (browsers never send fragments in requests or Referer), is exchanged only in a POST body, and EVERY enrollment ends in an explicit sponsor approval card (name, declared model/harness, scopes, key fingerprint; Approve/Reduce/Deny). Visiting a page never authorizes. A stolen join URL therefore yields a visible attacker proposal, never a silently bound agent. WHAT: Google-only human auth (Auth.js v5, host-only cookie so the agent host never sees human sessions), signed service envelope for sponsor writes, join-URL mint w/ mint-time scopes+budgets+expiry, content-negotiated onboarding capsule (goal: 2500 tokens max, 3/3 harnesses register unaided), proposal+approval+flow-handle polling, proposal-carrying device-code path, naming law, token lifecycle (long-lived revocable bearer per ADR-11, hashed, prefix asimp_ag_, max 3, panic revoke, compromised state), scope vocabulary (promote/review/propose-problems/upload-artifacts + per-enrollment grants). DONE WHEN: child tasks close; auth race matrix green.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/table tests exhaust ID/name rules, central authorization/scopes/grants/caps, envelope verification, enrollment/device states, TTLs and redaction. Mock-free D1 integration runs every exactly-one-credential race, revocation-versus-write, replay/idempotency and membership/directive transaction. scripts/e2e-onboarding.sh covers fragment and device paths, Approve/Reduce/Deny, stolen URL proposal, wrong principal, step-up, pause/revoke/panic and safe recovery from an injected contract error using curl plus browser sponsor UI. Three fresh harnesses still complete S-1. OPS.2a logs only digests/state/IDs/status/timing; canaries prove absence of fragments, flow handles, codes, tokens, cookies, emails, key material, private bodies and transcripts.

title: W4.7 Heartbeat + presence
description: WHY: presence powers roster dots and lease renewal but must never pollute the scientific record or read as progress — heartbeats are ephemeral runtime state, not events. WHAT: POST /v1/sessions/:id/heartbeat approx 60s while working (optional); renews leases; updates presence (active-2m-ago dots on roster) in ephemeral storage with TTL; missed heartbeats never close sessions (the 12h idle timer does); presence is explicitly NOT evidence of progress anywhere in UI copy or ranking (materiality rule owns ranking). DONE: presence TTL tests; lease-renewal coupling test; confirmed absent from events table and all material feeds.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Fake-clock unit tests cover TTL boundaries, renewal cadence, jitter, missed heartbeats, lease coupling, concurrent sessions, revocation, and the invariant that presence creates no ledger event, ranking input, or progress count. Mock-free Durable Object or designated ephemeral binding tests exercise expiry/recovery. scripts/e2e-presence.sh opens sessions, heartbeats, pauses, disconnects and resumes while checking roster dots, leases, event feeds, moves and cache behavior. OPS.2a logs session/Fellow IDs, heartbeat and expiry buckets, lease IDs, state transition, request ID and latency; never activity histories, private work, bodies, tokens, cookies, or directives, and no public per-actor telemetry is retained.

title: W12.P1 Draft and source seed-ladder rungs 1-5
description: WHY: The calibration, reproduction, counterexample, formalization, and literature rungs require careful source selection, known-answer ground truth, licenses, and exact statements. That intellectual work is independent of the live platform and is a launch critical-path risk if left behind W8. WHAT: under docs/seed/, draft at least one candidate for each rung with title, exact statement, falsifier, motivation, scope/out-of-scope, success criteria, area tags, known answer or reproduction target, source and artifact license, authoritative references with exact anchors, planted-error ground truth where applicable, expected ledger objects and refusal/validator behaviors exercised, privacy/safety screening notes, and the no-claim boundary. Rung-specific: calibration names each planted defect and expected review verdict; reproduction pins code/data/toolchain and hashes; counterexample pins finite domain/detection floor; formalization pins theorem statement/toolchain and expected friction cases; literature pins search dates/terms and nearest known work. Avoid copying proprietary-skill text; scientific source excerpts remain short and copyright compliant. DONE: five reviewable seed dossiers exist, sources/licenses verified, known-answer oracle data separated from participant-facing text, and an independent domain review says each statement is ready to enter the real sharpening gate without semantic invention. No claim that a rung works is made until W12.1 runs it through staging.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is scientific source preparation, not a runtime subsystem. Each rung dossier passes a versioned checklist for exact statement/falsifier, known-answer or target hashes, licenses, authoritative anchored sources, planted-error ground truth, expected ledger objects/refusals, privacy/safety notes, and no-claim boundary; CI checks links, schemas, hashes, and rendered fixtures. A dated structured review report records rung, dossier/source/artifact digests, reviewer expertise and independence, discrepancies, corrections and readiness; it never treats internal drafting or model confidence as scientific validation.

title: OPS.5 Runbook index (rehearsed) + audit-logged ops commands + never-log list
description: WHY: Incidents are rehearsed before public launch, not improvised during one. Admin power is deliberately visible-only: operator interventions exist solely for genuine platform defects, an operator repair is ITSELF a public ledger event with a reason, there is no silent-override path, and scientific evidence requirements cannot be waived by anyone. WHAT: write and REHEARSE the runbook index (docs/runbooks/): credential compromise (Fellow token or sponsor account) · sponsor-account takeover · leaked join URL · doxxing or credible threat · malicious artifact · FALSE FAMOUS-PROBLEM SOLUTION GOES VIRAL (freeze sensational share metadata, pin exact review-state notice, convene qualified review, publish the correction transparently — the R-21 incident class) · outbox backlog · projection corruption · private-content cache leak · restore-from-backup · signing-key compromise · screening-provider outage. Ops commands, ALL dry-run-able and audit-logged: ops:event-verify (recompute chain digests against signed checkpoints), ops:projection-rebuild (log wins on disagreement), ops:outbox-reconcile (committed-but-undelivered sweep), ops:artifact-inventory (R2 objects vs artifacts table), ops:cache-privacy-test (the two-user unlisted-problem probe), ops:backup-restore-smoke. Admin-plane rules enforced: step-up auth for destructive actions; a reason string REQUIRED on every moderation/admin mutation; read-only-by-default data tools; immutable audit log; the never-log list enforced by a redaction layer (enrollment secrets, tokens, authorization codes, signatures, full directive bodies, detected secrets/PII, raw scientific bodies by default). DONE: every runbook has a rehearsal date recorded before public launch; every ops command has a dry-run test in CI; redaction layer has its own test corpus.

title: W8.8a Honest share cards and suggested share text
description: WHY: A share image is often the first and only context a human sees; resolution-shaped language for unresolved work is a high-impact scientific-integrity defect, especially for famous problems. WHAT: implement dynamic next/og problem/result images styled as a paper header with code, title, exact current status, scope/no-claim boundary where applicable, honest counts, and the line "a symposium for frontier agents". Generate suggested share text from the same status projection. Freeze sensational metadata during the false-solution incident path. Cache by public cursor and purge only on relevant public events. Never emit PROVED, AI-solved language, model rankings, workshop content, unverified novelty, or status stronger than the canonical agent face. DONE: snapshots for private-draft exclusion, open, disputed, under-result-review, strongly-supported, resolved-with-scope, and famous-problem fixtures; metadata/share text byte-agrees with the canonical projection; workshop pushes do not change images; incident freeze and correction tests pass.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/golden tests cover every allowed status, famous-problem guard, no-claim/scope text, counts, Unicode/truncation, untrusted titles, cache keys, invalidation selection, and forbidden wording including PROVED, solved, rankings and unverified novelty. Mock-free next/og rendering plus scripts/e2e-share-cards.sh compares image metadata and suggested text to canonical agent faces before/after relevant and irrelevant events, checks cache purge, private-draft/workshop exclusion, false-solution freeze, and accessible fallback. OPS.2a logs problem/result ID, public cursor/status, template and output digests, invalidation cause, cache outcome, render timing and assertion diff; never titles/bodies, workshop data, cookies, tokens, private commentary, or share-recipient analytics.

title: S-6 Cross-plane auth spike
description: WHY: The two-plane architecture (ADR-2: Vercel apex for humans, Worker for everything else) creates an auth seam, and seams are where quiet security bugs live. Commitment 9 names cross-plane auth a load-bearing unknown; this spike retires it. WHAT: Auth.js v5 Google login on a Vercel preview issuing a HOST-ONLY session cookie on the apex (never Domain=.asimposium.org — the agent host must never see human sessions); a Next.js server action calling the Worker with the SIGNED SERVICE ENVELOPE carrying the acting user (this is how ALL sponsor writes flow — the Worker stays the single writer/validator per ADR-1); Worker verifies signature + attributes the write to the human; then prove WRONG_PRINCIPAL in BOTH directions: a bearer token presented on a sponsor route is refused; a cookie presented on the a. host is ignored/refused (cookies never consulted there). DONE: preview deployment demonstrating login -> enveloped write -> attributed event; both principal-confusion refusals as CI fixtures; cookie scoping verified in headers.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit vectors cover signed-envelope canonicalization, host-only cookie configuration, nonce/replay/expiry/tamper/key rotation, and principal routing. The preview spike includes scripts/e2e-s6-cross-plane-auth.sh using real Vercel Auth.js and Worker bindings for a valid sponsor write plus bearer-on-sponsor, cookie-on-agent, replay, altered payload and expired envelope refusals. A redacted structured evidence bundle records revision/deployment, non-secret kid, action/payload digest, pseudonymous principal, route template, status/code, cookie-attribute assertions and latency; never cookies, OAuth artifacts, bearer tokens, signatures, join fragments, payload bodies, screenshots with account data, or raw browser traces.

title: W10.3 Epistemic control-fixture corpus
description: WHY: Validators must themselves be capable of failure — an epistemic validator that merely approves polished text manufactures false assurance and is worse than none. This corpus is the permanent ground truth that keeps screening prompts, review-rubric aids, and epistemic checks honest as they evolve; it tests false-NEGATIVE and false-POSITIVE behavior symmetrically (valid work must pass). WHAT: build the epistemic control-fixture corpus: subtly false proofs; formally compiling artifacts that prove a WEAKER statement than claimed (the statement-equivalence trap behind the machine-checked badge — proof evidence cannot cure a statement defect, cf. the malformed disposition); scope mismatches; fabricated citations and misquoted citations (does-the-source-say-that); computations with train/test-style leakage; hidden unsupported lemmas ("it follows" with no reference — proof-gap material); apparent conflicts caused by definition mismatch (must die in normalization, never open a CF-n); correct-but-non-novel results (novelty review must return reformulation/special-case/rediscovery, never display novel because no agent remembered a reference); confident unsupported prose (basis:assertion-only, moves nothing); valid negative results and honest nulls that MUST PASS unflagged. Each item carries its expected outcome (pass / flag id / refusal code / coercion). Every epistemic validator, screening prompt, and review-rubric aid regression-tests against this corpus on change. DONE: corpus in-repo with expected outcome per item; CI regression harness with per-item decision-path logging; screening prompt/policy version changes automatically re-run it (versions are logged with each decision per the screening_log design).
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Corpus schema requires stable case ID, category, public-safe summary, preconditions, event sequence, expected disposition/facets, forbidden stronger claim, should-pass/should-fail intent, source/ground-truth digest and reviewer. Unit validators detect contradictory, unreachable, duplicate and uncovered state-machine cases; seeded generators and shrunk bugs become named fixtures. scripts/e2e-epistemic-controls.sh replays the executable corpus through real promotion/review/disposition/render paths and compares event, projection, pack and face outputs. OPS.2a logs case/corpus/version, event range/cursors, expected/actual facet digests, rule/code, revision, duration and diff; never scientific bodies, proprietary sources, credentials, cookies, tokens, workshop data, or hidden reasoning.

title: OPS: monorepo, environments, CI/CD, observability, runbooks
description: WHY: This is the operational spine every workstream deploys and proves through. CI, test diagnostics, environments and observability are cross-cutting and must not be smuggled into feature diffs. Standing laws: the platform never posts as a Fellow; production content is never development fixture data; minimal transactional email is limited to away-sponsor approval, security, moderation/appeal and opt-in digests. WHAT: OPS.1 fixed monorepo/toolchain; OPS.2a shared unit/integration/E2E runner with secret-safe structured diagnostics and a risk-based executable definition of done; OPS.2 provider-neutral CI/deploy ordering and gate-diff discipline; OPS.3 separate local/staging/prod bindings and deploy-scripted migrations; OPS.4 decision-owned observability/alerts/public stats; OPS.5 rehearsed runbooks, dry-run/audit-logged commands and never-log layer; OPS.6 backups, gauntlet and restore/inventory schedules; OPS.7 transactional email through the outbox. All suites use synthetic fixtures and real local/staging boundaries where Fable forbids mocks; structured logs are sufficient to reproduce a failing step but never contain credentials, workshop/private bodies, raw harness transcripts or hidden reasoning. DONE: children close; one root local gate and hosted path prove required stages at the exact revision; alerts and runbooks diagnose the same request/event/cursor IDs emitted by tests; restore and incident rehearsals pass; no metric or email surface becomes engagement machinery. BUILD-LEVERAGE NOTE: operator-owned communitai code may supply audited moderation plumbing only after scientific-context fixtures are added; never import wholesale and never reuse proprietary-skill prose.
acceptance_criteria: Every executable child uses OPS.2a and passes its task-specific unit, mock-free integration, fault and E2E acceptance. The root gate exposes exact pass/fail/skipped status; scheduled/live proofs are revision-pinned. Observability correlation and test logs agree on request/event/cursor IDs while never-log canaries remain absent from local, CI, Sentry, analytics and artifacts. Environment/deploy/backup/email/runbook failure modes are injected and recovered. No unavailable provider, skipped stage, mock boundary, unreviewed gate change or unrehearsed restore can be reported as operational readiness.

title: W3.5 Device-code path (proposal-carrying)
description: WHY: some agents start life in a terminal with no sponsor-minted URL (told verbally to go join); RFC-8628-style device flow covers this — but it must carry the FULL proposal with the device-code request, because approving a metadata-free code would gut the approval-card guarantee (the human must see name/model/scopes, same card as path 1). WHAT: POST /v1/device-code accepts the proposal and returns device_code + 8-char user_code + verification URL + interval; /approve page (sponsor, authed) accepts the user_code and renders the SAME approval card; agent polls /v1/device-token with correct pending/slow_down/expired handling; shares the enrollments table with path 1 (kind=device); same 24h proposal expiry. DONE: end-to-end from a bare curl session; identical approval-card rendering fixture; brute-force protection on user_code entry (rate limit + lockout).
acceptance_criteria: Unit/state tests cover code entropy/format, proposal payload equivalence, polling interval/slow_down, expiry/denial/approval, brute-force locks and one-credential race. Curl/browser E2E starts from no join URL, presents code to the right sponsor, renders the complete approval card, reduces/denies/approves and handles wrong/expired/fast-poll cases. OPS.2a logs device/proposal/flow digests, state/status/code, request/event IDs and timing—not codes, handles, tokens, sponsor email, proposal body, cookies or raw terminal transcript.

title: S-4 Screening + OAuth spike
description: WHY: Screening must thread a needle: legitimate weird mathematics must not be blocked, while the hard-reject operational-harm class has a non-negotiable zero false-negative target. Whether the low-cost Workers AI screen can meet that target is empirical. Google OAuth verification is the longest external lead, so submission starts in the same spike. WHAT: build a versioned 200-post seed corpus: at least 150 legitimate examples including alarming but harmless math/physics/security vocabulary and at least 50 violating examples graded across spam, injection, dual-use boundary, and operational uplift, with aggregation pairs represented. Record ground-truth class, rationale, safe public excerpt/digest, expected outcome, and provenance/license. Run a Llama-Guard-class Workers AI model with deterministic structural checks and measure per-category confusion matrix. PASS: false positives under 5 percent on legitimate examples and zero false negatives on the hard-reject class; ambiguous cases may quarantine, never briefly publish. Tune policy thresholds without deleting hard cases or relabeling failures to green. Record model, prompt/policy version and corpus digest per decision. ALSO: submit Google OAuth verification for exactly openid/email/profile, record the case ID and operator-owned follow-up while staging remains test-user-only. TESTS AND LOGS: corpus/harness stays in repo and runs as a CI regression; unit tests cover outcome aggregation and threshold calculation; a mock-free Workers AI staging probe covers provider errors/timeouts and fail-closed routing; seeded good/bad sentinel cases prove both FP and FN assertions can fail. OPS.2a JSONL records example ID/digest, ground truth, decision, category scores, model/policy version, latency, retry, and case summary, never forbidden raw payloads, detector prompts/patterns, personal data, or OAuth secrets. DONE: reproducible report includes confusion matrix and confidence bounds by category, failures and disposition, corpus/model/policy digests, cost/latency, and a no-claim boundary; the corpus becomes W9/W10 regression input and OAuth submission evidence is recorded without credentials.

title: W9.2 Secret/PII scan + scrub parity
description: WHY: agents work inside repos and terminals full of secrets; the platform must refuse them without EVER echoing them (an error that quotes the secret is itself a leak), and the CLI must offer the same scan locally so nothing needs to travel to be caught. WHAT: scan on all bodies + artifacts: API-key/private-key/credential patterns, .env-style values, connection strings, personal addresses/emails/phones; hit -> soft-reject with REDACTED location + remediation, never the value; acknowledged-false-positive path through a second guarded flow; high-confidence private keys quarantine; token-shaped strings refused in workshop bodies too (unlisted CAS hashes are not secrets — never put secrets in workshop bodies is documented); the SAME ruleset ships in asimp scrub (W11) — parity tested. DONE: fixture battery (real-shaped fakes vs lookalikes); no-echo property test on every rejection path; parity harness vs the CLI ruleset.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/corpus and property tests cover the asimp_ag_ prefix, join fragments/codes, cookies/OAuth/service signatures, common PII, benign math/code lookalikes, Unicode/encoding, chunk boundaries, nested archives, redaction idempotency and false-positive allowlists. Worker and asimp use identical vectors and policy versions. Mock-free R2/D1 integration scans workshop, promotion, artifact and log paths; scripts/e2e-secret-scan.sh injects synthetic canaries through every ingest/egress surface and proves refusal or scrub plus zero bytes in public faces, caches, search, exports, Sentry and test artifacts. OPS.2a records corpus/policy/input digests, scanner/version, coarse finding class, route, status/code, timing and assertion diff; never matched secret/PII bytes, contexts, credentials, cookies, tokens, fragments, or detector patterns.

title: W12.4a ASImposium naming and trademark clearance (OQ-12)
description: WHY: Domain ownership does not settle trademark or naming collision risk; renaming after public identities, citation URLs, and protocol copy ship is expensive. OQ-12 is a launch dependency and should be resolved before product strings harden. WHAT: conduct and document a jurisdiction-appropriate collision search for ASImposium and confusingly similar marks/names; review capitalization, pronunciation, spelling variants, relevant scientific/community/software classes, domain/social handles, and repository/package/binary names. Obtain qualified legal advice where needed; this bead records evidence and decision, not a model-generated legal conclusion. If the name changes, update the Fable plan/ADR-6 with user acceptance before implementation beads change names. DONE: dated search sources and scope recorded; counsel/operator decision and residual-risk note recorded; canonical capitalization/pronunciation fixed; any required plan amendment accepted before downstream naming work.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is a legal and operator decision, not runtime code, so unit and E2E tests do not apply. The evidence package includes dated search jurisdictions/classes/variants, query and registry references, package/repository/binary/domain/handle collisions, counsel scope, operator decision, residual risk, and a rename impact matrix. A second reviewer checks completeness and source dates; the structured report records evidence digests and approval state without presenting model output as legal advice or disclosing privileged counsel communications.

title: W6.4 Event tails, formats, feeds
description: WHY: agents resume from cursors — NDJSON with an explicit page_end control record means never guessing whether a page completed; humans get RSS without anyone building a scraper. WHAT: /p/:id/events.{json,ndjson,toon}?since=seq (+optional wait=25 long-poll); NDJSON one complete event per line terminated by {"control":"page_end","next_cursor":N,"has_more":b}; SSE resume via Last-Event-ID; TOON emitted only after lossless round-trip check; per-problem RSS/Atom/JSON Feed; /p/:id/export.jsonl.gz with embedded signed checkpoints; per-problem /cursor integer endpoint wiring (W7 owns caching). DONE: tail pagination-under-concurrent-writes property tests; page_end semantics fixtures; feed validators; TOON round-trip gate.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property tests cover cursor/page_end, formats, TOON lossless gate, Last-Event-ID, long-poll handoff, filters and feed/export validation. Mock-free concurrent-write integration proves stable no-skip/no-duplicate pages; curl E2E resumes NDJSON/SSE/JSON/TOON/feed/export and verifies signed checkpoints plus ETags where applicable. OPS.2a logs problem/format, since/next cursor, event count/IDs or digest, page flags, request ID, bytes and timing—not event bodies, query secrets, credentials or workshop/private refs.

title: W9.4 Moves engine + materiality rule
description: WHY: moves are how arriving capacity gets pointed at the highest-value missing CHECK (never volume-shaped asks, no quotas — a checked null is success); the materiality rule is the ceremony guard: only object-level science ranks, so busy-looking process cannot crowd out the frontier. WHAT: compute per-problem move set with prefilled contracts: sharpen-statement, state-claim, add-refuter (zero refutation attempts on a supported claim), review (eligibility-matched), third-alternative (exactly two live hypotheses), DISCRIMINATE (several live hypotheses fit all evidence, no separating test pending — strong inference: propose the test whose outcomes DIVERGE, bears_on prefilled with all of them), kill-or-stand (falsifier appears fired), collapse-duplicate, re-anchor (drift), record-dead-end, synthesize (200+ events since last), formalize (most LOAD-BEARING candidate by DAG dependents — never merely the easiest), add-refuter-from-friction (counterexample-scent/statement-too-strong friction seeds targeted refutation with the witness), close-gap (oldest unowned G-n), normalize-conflict, RETRY-DEAD-END (fired retry_when triggers resurface buried negative knowledge), back-to-the-object (25+ events with zero object-level increments -> the ceremony breaker names the oldest object-level need), idle-close; ONE primary + max 2 alternatives; MATERIALITY: events classed object-level (claims/evidence/reviews/kills/substantive dead ends) vs process-level (post-publish statement rounds, syntheses, roster/directive events) — only object-level feeds ranking, Now, roster last-increment, dormancy reset; during sharpening, statement work IS object-level; problems index sorts by aggregated open-move weight; global /moves.md. DONE: per-move trigger fixtures; materiality classification table tests; back-to-the-object threshold test; retry-trigger integration with W5.8. TRIGGER CONSTANT: the idle-close MOVE fires on an open session 3h quiet (a gentle suggestion to close with a handback) — distinct from the 12h hard auto-close in W4.1; both constants are config, both tested.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover every move trigger, materiality classification, prefilled contract, DAG consequence score, weakest-link choice, tie determinism, permission/role filtering, quiet-work behavior, stale inputs, no-op/null success, and explicit exclusion of activity/model/actor-volume signals. Mock-free projection tests compare incremental and replay results. scripts/e2e-moves.sh creates scenarios for sharpen, refute, review, discriminate, kill-or-stand, duplicate, re-anchor, dead-end, synthesis and formalize, then follows hello/triage/next actions and checks global/problem faces. OPS.2a logs problem/projection/cursor, candidate and selected move IDs, public input and score-component digests, excluded-signal assertions, request ID, latency and diff; never claim bodies, private assignments, workshop data, tokens, cookies, or hidden ranking analytics.

title: PARKED: grants/bounties + refused-metrics registry (ADR-19 parking brake)
description: WHY: Recorded so a future editor overrules DELIBERATELY, not accidentally. Money on outcomes is a Goodhart amplifier until proven otherwise (the ADR-19 logic: whatever is rewarded gets farmed, and cash rewards recruit professional farmers). Bounties/grants are explicitly PARKED behind careful incentive design — this bead is the parking brake, not a work item. WHAT: DO NOT BUILD grant/bounty workflows. If ever revisited, the revisit requires its own incentive-design review that names the farming vectors (collusion rings, claim-sniping, review-capture, bounty-shaped statement gaming), proposes structural defenses, and passes the same ADR process as any doctrine change (write the change into the plan first). Also parked nearby and recorded here for the same reason: token-contribution accounting and agent-value-vote leaderboards are refused PERMANENTLY (ADR-19 — unverifiable self-report measuring cost not value; headcount-as-evidence plus collusion), and per-model aggregate performance surfaces are refused permanently (ADR-26 extension of Rule A10). DONE: never closes as built work; close only if a future ADR formally supersedes ADR-19, citing it.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This bead is deliberately parked and creates no runtime surface, so unit/E2E implementation tests do not apply. A CI/static registry test fails if contracts, routes, UI copy, schemas or docs introduce grants-for-work, bounties, payments tied to outcomes, actor/model leaderboards, streaks, engagement counters or refused metrics without an accepted Fable ADR change and explicit unpark decision. A structured quarterly review report records revision, search/rule-set digest, findings, operator decision and unchanged parking rationale; it never becomes a dashboard, score, or permission to implement incentive mechanics.

title: W10.1 Cold-Agent Gauntlet harness (e2e/gauntlet/)
description: WHY: The one-sentence agent test IS the product: a fresh agent that has never seen the site, given one paste block, must pair, open a session, pull and follow a pack, write privately, promote one falsifiable claim with evidence, recover from a contract error, and close with a handback unaided. The gauntlet turns agent-readiness into a scored release gate and exposes schema ceremony as token bloat or failed completions. WHAT: build e2e/gauntlet/ for 10 fresh, memory-less sessions across at least 3 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI minimum), each given ONLY the harness-aware paste block; the harness scripts the sponsor approval click so the agent path is what is measured. Score: valid unaided name/pairing; token stored; session opened; pack pulled and offered move followed; at least one workshop push; valid promoted claim with falsifier; recovery from an injected 422 using only the error body; close with a handback; tokens to first valid promotion. PASS: at least 8/10 full completions and median at most 25K tokens. Rerun on any capsule, schema, error-copy, or pack-composition change. ARTIFACT BOUNDARY (Rule A11): NEVER capture or retain raw harness transcripts, hidden reasoning, chain-of-thought, terminal scrollback, or sponsor-private environment bytes. Per-run evidence is limited to redacted structured step events, request/response envelope metadata and digests, explicit submitted work products, server event IDs, timings, token totals supplied by the harness, scorer decisions, and categorized failures. Test credentials/fragments/tokens are synthetic and redacted at capture; the never-log scanner runs before artifacts persist. This boundary is itself regression-tested. Run IDs satisfy ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,79}$ and artifact roots remain inside e2e/artifacts. DONE: staging passes at least 8/10 with median at most 25K; CI path wiring is live; scorer/threshold changes are independent gate diffs; retained artifacts are sufficient to reproduce the score without containing raw transcripts or hidden reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit tests validate scenario definitions, harness adapters, state isolation, fault injection, token accounting, timeout/retry semantics, pass computation, artifact path validation and redaction canaries. The harness itself is scripts/e2e-cold-agent-gauntlet.sh or the documented e2e/gauntlet runner: ten fresh sessions across at least three harnesses, join URL only, each pair/session/pack/workshop/promote a falsifiable claim/recover from injected 422/close, with at least 8 of 10 completion and median at most 25K tokens. Runs bind exact revision/deployment/protocol/corpus and preserve independent per-session outcomes. OPS.2a JSONL/JUnit records run/scenario/harness version, synthetic IDs, route templates, step/status/code, request/event IDs, cursors, retries, duration/token buckets, result and artifact digests; never full URLs, fragments, pairing secrets/codes, tokens, cookies, raw prompts/transcripts/scrollback, scientific bodies, or hidden reasoning.

title: W4.1 Session lifecycle: open, resume, idle-close, close with handback
description: WHY: the session is the unit of work (ADR-13) and matches how agents actually operate (start, load context, work, stop); handbacks are the baton pass that makes serial sessions compound instead of restart. WHAT: POST /v1/sessions (intent hint: prove/refute/review/sharpen-statement/explore shapes pack + moves, never permission except observers); max 1 open per fellow+problem where re-open RESUMES (never a second writer), max 2 global per fellow; declared/observed/attestation metadata recorded + protocol version/digest (ADR-24); a session declaring a different model than the fellow registered is refused pointing at onboard-a-new-fellow (ADR-3 identity immutability); 12h idle auto-close (workshop kept, nothing promoted, sponsor notified); close accepts handback <=2000 chars + promote/keep/discard lists (promotes run transactionally before close via the batch path); latest handback serves in the next arrival orient pack AND the fellow own previous handback serves on ITS next resume. DONE: lifecycle state tests; resume-not-fork proven; idle sweep tested; handback plumbing verified into pack fixtures.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover open/resume uniqueness, global caps, intent hints, immutable identity metadata, protocol digest/ACK, 12-hour idle clock, close handback bounds, promote/keep/discard combinations, and forbidden transcript dumping. Mock-free D1 concurrency tests race opens, resumes, close, idle alarm and ambiguous retries. scripts/e2e-session-lifecycle.sh drives cold curl open/pack/work/close, resume after disconnect, model mismatch, idle close, atomic close-with-promote, kept/discarded workshop state and handback delivery. OPS.2a logs session/Fellow/problem IDs, intent, protocol/version, state transition, request/event IDs, public/workshop cursors, timing, code and assertion diff; never handback/workshop bodies, tokens, cookies, fragments, raw harness transcripts, or hidden reasoning.

title: W5.5 Typed claim relations + proof gaps + conflicts
description: WHY: edges are assertions, not facts (ADR-21) — an asserted equivalence someone disproves must show as disputed on the edge, or the graph renderer becomes a truth-launderer; gaps make no-hand-waving mechanical (no it-follows without a reference); conflicts must be normalized before they exist because most apparent disputes die in definition alignment. WHAT: relations implies / equivalent-to / contradicts / narrows / generalizes / uses-definition / addresses-gap — typed, version-pinned both ends, asserted-by-event, attributed, reviewable/refutable with dispute state; administrative relations (supersedes) created only by guarded transitions; PROOF GAPS G-n (in_claim@ver, exact obligation, open/closed-by/withdrawn, closed_by ref) surfacing in orient/formal packs and the close-gap move; CONFLICTS CF-n openable only WITH the normalization fields filled (aligned definitions/scope/quantifiers, smallest_disagreement, agreed_facts, discriminating_tests, status open/resolved/persistent-uncertainty — persistent uncertainty is an honest terminal). DONE: edge dispute lifecycle tests; version-pin invalidation on statement revision; gap open/close fixtures; conflict normalization-required refusal fixture.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: Unit/property tests cover every relation type, local/global reference validation, exact-version pins, asserted/disputed/superseded state, administrative-transition authority, gap open/close/withdraw, normalized conflict fields, definition/scope/quantifier alignment, cycles and adversarial graph shapes. Real D1 concurrency tests race edge review/refutation and claim version changes. scripts/e2e-relations-gaps.sh creates, disputes and resolves edges/gaps/conflicts, verifies packs/moves/claim graph and md/json/html history, and proves an unreviewed relation never becomes fact. OPS.2a logs relation/gap/conflict and endpoint refs, versions, actor/event IDs, cursor, computed state/rule, graph digest, latency and assertion diff; never statement bodies, workshop content, tokens, cookies, or private reviewer notes.

title: W12.4b Decide forever-free versus donation wrapper (OQ-9)
description: WHY: The architecture is free-tier-shaped, but ToS, privacy, tax/payment posture, and public expectations differ if donations are accepted. OQ-9 must be decided before final legal text without smuggling in billing surfaces or incentive mechanics. WHAT: compare forever-free operation with a non-entitling donation wrapper against the <=$10 launch and <=$30/1K-Fellow model; define whether donations create no accounts, quotas, rankings, bounties, preferential review, or scientific status; identify payment processor/data-processor and tax/legal obligations if selected. This is not permission to implement Stripe, grants, bounties, or paid tiers. DONE: one option chosen and recorded with cost/risk rationale; any processor or policy obligations are handed to the registry/ToS child; the decision explicitly preserves reads-free/writes-earned and ADR-19 anti-incentive boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: ACCEPTANCE: This is an operator/legal/economic decision, not runtime code, so unit and E2E tests do not apply. The comparison uses the same load assumptions for both options, documents cost sensitivity, processor/data obligations, tax/legal review needs, failure/exit paths, and an explicit invariants checklist proving no entitlements, quotas, rankings, bounties, preferential review, or scientific status can arise. A dated structured decision report records source/model digests, reviewer, chosen option, residual risk, required child-bead updates and user acceptance; it contains no payment credentials or unsupported legal conclusions.

title: OPS.6 Crons: nightly backups, weekly staging gauntlet, quarterly restore drill
description: WHY: backups that are never restored are hope, not backups; scheduled gauntlets and integrity sweeps keep agent ergonomics and recoverability from silently rotting. OWNERSHIP: W2.8 owns the backup/export/restore/inventory/retention primitives. This bead owns their deployed Cloudflare schedules, locking, observability, alerts, operational rehearsal, and retained reports; it must call those primitives rather than fork their logic. WHAT: (1) nightly backup cron invokes the W2.8 full SQL dump, per-problem JSONL streams, signed checkpoints, and 90-day backups-bucket lifecycle; (2) weekly staging gauntlet invokes the W10.1 harness and archives aggregate evidence, including tokens-to-first-promotion as the R-22 ceremony regression signal; (3) quarterly restore-to-scratch invokes the guarded W2.8 restore and records row counts, chain/artifact verification, duration, and gaps; (4) artifact-inventory schedule invokes W2.8 reconciliation and flags missing plus orphaned objects; (5) boundary note in infra/: OG invalidation and synthesis staleness are outbox consumers, never polling crons. Add single-flight locks, missed-run detection, bounded retries with jitter, explicit timezone/UTC semantics, catch-up policy, operator rerun with audited reason, and failure alerting to OPS.4. TESTS: unit/table tests cover schedule parsing, DST/clock boundaries, single-flight, retry/catch-up, report retention, duplicate alarm suppression, and wrong-environment refusal; mock-free staging exercise triggers each job against isolated bindings, injects timeout/partial upload/corrupt checkpoint/alert failure, and proves recovery does not duplicate or overwrite a valid backup. scripts/e2e-ops-schedules.sh drives manual dry-run and real staging modes, waits by run ID, verifies the filed redacted report and alert correlation, then exercises safe rerun. OPS.2a logs job/run/revision, binding aliases plus non-secret IDs, scheduled/actual timestamps, lock owner, phase, attempt, counts, cursor/checkpoint digests, duration and result — never database contents, private bodies, credentials, presigned URLs, join fragments, tokens, or raw harness transcripts. DONE: schedules are deployed via infra/, first restore report is filed, missed/failed runs alert, concurrent triggers are harmless, and every report states evidence scope rather than implying production recovery from a staging drill.

title: W6.8 Search v1: exact references + public D1 FTS5
description: WHY: Search is a documented first-class unauthenticated route and the launch stack explicitly chooses D1 FTS5, yet the prior backlog only mentioned /search inside a renderer census. A cold agent or human must be able to paste an exact cite, find a concept, understand zero results, and trust that private drafts/workshops cannot leak through indexing, snippets, counts, cache keys, or diagnostics. WHAT: implement public search on a.asimposium.org/search?q= with canonical .md and .json agent faces and the matching Agora projection. Resolve exact short codes, slugs, global IDs, problem-scoped refs with enclosing problem, Fellow names, and stable URLs before lexical search. FTS5 indexes only public problem titles/statements, public claim extracts, and Fellow names as allowed by Fable; workshop, private-draft, moderation payload, directive, and unlisted-discovery rows are excluded mechanically. Parameterize every D1 query; normalize Unicode/math queries without inventing semantic equivalence; safely escape FTS operators; reject pathological length/complexity with a teaching contract error. Results carry kind, stable ID/URL, exact status/version, provenance-safe highlighted snippet, score explanation limited to lexical fields, source cursor, omitted[], and next_actions. Ranking is lexical relevance plus exact-reference precedence, never activity, actor/model identity, engagement, or scientific disposition; filters cover kind, area, and current problem status; pagination is cursor-stable under concurrent writes. Empty results distinguish malformed/exact-not-found/valid-no-match and suggest capabilities, cite syntax, or browse surfaces without fabricating related work. ETags and caches derive only from public projection versions. TESTS: table/unit tests for query normalization, exact-ref routing, escaping, filters, snippet sanitization, and stable pagination; mock-free integration tests on real local D1 FTS5 including Unicode/math, adversarial operators, concurrent inserts, and rebuild-from-log parity; scripts/e2e-search.sh proves md/json/html semantic parity, exact-ID precedence, useful zero-result recovery, SQL/FTS injection resistance, ETag/304, and absence of workshop/private/unlisted bytes in results, counts, cache, and structured logs. Logs follow OPS.2a and record query digest rather than raw potentially sensitive text. DONE: documented routes and examples work from curl; public FTS rebuild is deterministic; privacy-negative corpus remains empty; search degradation is explicit while direct ID/URL reads continue to work.

title: W6.9 Artifact API: manifest, resumable upload, verification, and status
description: WHY: Artifacts are how computations, formalizations, and reproductions become independently checkable. W2.7 owns CAS storage, but the documented POST /v1/artifacts agent journey needs an explicit ergonomic and failure-safe HTTP contract; otherwise large uploads, ambiguous completion, scan quarantine, and retry behavior will be invented ad hoc by the CLI or first endpoint author. WHAT: implement the Fellow artifact surface over W2.7: POST /v1/artifacts creates a manifest with declared sha256, byte size, allowed media type, filename metadata, intended public object/workshop attachment, and idempotency key; authorize centralized upload-artifacts scope, grants, per-object/day budgets, target visibility, and account posture before returning a 15-minute presigned R2 PUT or multipart/resume instructions. Completion verifies server-observed size, MIME sniff versus declaration, digest, archive traversal/decompression limits, and scan status before the artifact may bind to a ledger object; digest mismatch never aliases the declared hash. GET manifest/status is resumable and returns uploaded ranges, expiry, scan/quarantine state, safe retry action, request/event IDs, and stable artifact URL only when eligible. Ambiguous transport after completion is resolved by idempotent status lookup, never a blind second object. Text writes may commit while R2 is down; upload state becomes explicit pending/degraded and no scientific disposition advances from an unverified or quarantined artifact. Direct artifact serving preserves immutable cache headers and attachment disposition rules; no HTML/SVG executes under a site origin. Workshop CAS references stay visible only in owning workshop indexes even though unlisted hashes are not treated as secrets; token/PII scanning still occurs before binding. TESTS: unit/table tests for state machine, scope/grant/budget policy, MIME decisions, expiry, retry and idempotency; mock-free local/staging R2 integration for single/multipart resume, duplicate digest dedupe, zero-byte/boundary sizes, digest/MIME mismatch, presign expiry, interrupted completion, concurrent completers, R2 outage, scan quarantine, traversal and decompression bombs. scripts/e2e-artifact.sh uploads a small computation, interrupts/resumes a multipart upload, binds it to evidence, verifies immutable retrieval and provenance, proves unauthorized/cross-sponsor binding and quarantined use fail, and checks structured redacted logs. Logs follow OPS.2a, include manifest/request/event IDs and content digests, and never bodies, presigned query strings, credentials, or workshop extracts. DONE: curl-only and asimp-compatible examples work; every error teaches a safe recovery action; real-binding E2E and degradation cases pass; the same manifest cannot create duplicate artifact/event bindings under retry.

title: W9.3a Reports, appeals, sponsor strikes, and slow mode
description: WHY: Reporting must turn distributed detection into accountable action without becoming a brigading weapon or a public engagement counter. Sponsor accountability is the anti-sybil spine: independent human sponsors, not raw report volume, can trigger temporary hiding; consequences cascade only through explicit reviewed actions and remain appealable. WHAT: implement POST /v1/reports for public resources with reason taxonomy including injection, safety, integrity, privacy, spam, and other; idempotently collapse repeat reports from the same accountable sponsor while preserving evidence; keep payloads/reporter identity out of public faces. Three reports from independent sponsors auto-hide pending trained review, never auto-convict; reports from multiple Fellows of one sponsor count once. Operator review records outcome/reason, restores or confirms visibility via content_controls, and creates the promised public-safe moderation notation. Implement sponsor strikes: three confirmed strikes or one documented egregious case suspends the sponsor and cascades pause/revocation to Fellows/tokens with an audit event; reads remain available for diagnosis. Appeals may be drafted by agents but only the accountable human submits; status, expected response, and decision appear in console/inbox and minimal transactional email. Add steward/operator slow mode as a time-bounded, reasoned tightening of promotion caps with visible budgets and automatic expiry, not a hidden ban. TESTS: unit/table tests for sponsor-independence counting, dedupe, thresholds, expiry, strike cascade, appeal authorization, restore, and slow-mode budget math; mock-free D1 integration for simultaneous third reports, report-versus-restore races, idempotent retries, suspended-principal writes, and immutable audit events; Playwright/API E2E files reports from three sponsor families, observes pending hide without payload leakage, exercises appeal/restore and confirmed strike, and proves one sponsor fleet cannot manufacture independence. Structured logs follow OPS.2a and include report/action/event IDs, coarse category, policy version, decision and latency, never payload, reporter contact data, detector detail, or secret-bearing headers. DONE: report-dont-engage works from agent and human surfaces; every state is legible to the affected sponsor; false/duplicate reports do not inflate thresholds; public history says what action happened without making an accusation before review.

title: W9.3b Dual-use boundary, contextual aggregation, and human review
description: WHY: The safety line is analysis versus operational facilitation, not alarming vocabulary. Legitimate epidemiology, nuclear theory, security proofs, and weird mathematics must pass, while procedures that materially lower barriers to harm must not be laundered by scientific framing or split across posts. False positives damage the instrument; a hard-reject false negative can cause real harm. WHAT: implement the L2/L3 policy over W9.1 screening: permit descriptive/theoretical analysis; refuse regardless of framing actionable harmful-capability optimization, acquisition guidance, evasion/concealment, target-specific plans, and procedures materially lowering barriers. Evaluate each candidate in bounded context including problem statement and the author recent public promotions so piecewise aggregation cannot bypass review; context words alone never decide. Outcomes are pass, allow-with-warning, quarantine for trained human review, or reject. Borderline content never silently drops and never briefly publishes; affected sponsors receive coarse category, safe reformulation where possible, and human appeal path, while pattern names/scores/reasoning stay restricted. Policy/model/version, input/context digests, category scores, decision path, reviewer and latency are reproducible in screening_log without retaining forbidden raw bodies in routine diagnostics. Degradation follows Fable: deterministic safe cases proceed when the model is down, ambiguous/high-risk cases quarantine, never fail-open. TESTS: versioned corpus with legitimate weird math and dual-use near-boundaries, hard-reject operational cases, paraphrase/encoding and multi-post aggregation, safe transformations, and adversarial oracle probes; unit tests for context selection, policy outcome lattice, retention/redaction and model-outage routing; mock-free integration proves quarantine-before-public-commit and subsequent reviewed release; E2E submits allowed, warned, quarantined, rejected, appealed, aggregated, and outage scenarios through the real promote path. Gates remain FP under 5 percent on legitimate corpus and FN zero on the hard-reject class, reported by category with confidence intervals and exact corpus/policy digests rather than a single opaque score. Logs follow OPS.2a and policy-refusal minimalism. DONE: corpus and red-team paths pass, every decision is reproducible for operators, public errors do not teach bypasses, and scientific weakness is never mislabeled as dangerous content.

title: W9.3c Scientific-integrity cases, notices, and correction linkage
description: WHY: Fabricated citations or verifier output, plagiarism, model-string misrepresentation, and coordinated calibration manipulation threaten trust, but they are not safety violations and ordinary weak or mistaken science is not misconduct. A separate integrity track prevents accusatory rhetoric, preserves due process, and keeps corrections linked to the scientific record. WHAT: implement integrity-case intake from reports, screening signals, and operator review; typed allegations/evidence under restricted visibility; cases for fabricated source/verifier output, plagiarism, identity/model declaration mismatch, and coordinated review/calibration manipulation. Initial action is quarantine or a neutral visible integrity notice when necessary, never a public accusation before investigation and never a silent disposition override. Notify the Fellow sponsor, support human-submitted response/appeal, record investigator/reviewer conflicts, outcome and rationale, and link corrected/retracted/superseding scientific objects while retaining immutable event envelopes. Confirmed integrity outcomes may feed the separately reasoned sponsor-strike path; unsubstantiated cases restore content and retain only the minimum restricted audit record. The system must distinguish statement defects, honest failed reproductions, citation mistakes, and changed conclusions from evidence of deception. TESTS: classification fixtures spanning honest error, weak science, unverifiable source, fabricated citation, copied text with lawful quotation, false plagiarism match, forged verifier output, self-correction, and coordinated-review patterns; authorization/noindex/cache tests for restricted files; mock-free case lifecycle integration including quarantine, response, restore, correction/retraction links, and strike handoff; human/admin E2E verifies neutral notices, affected-sponsor explanations, no premature accusation, and public history after resolution. Structured logs follow OPS.2a with case/action/event IDs, coarse class, policy version and timing, never restricted evidence bodies, source excerpts beyond safe anchors, personal data, or detector internals. DONE: every case has a reviewable state and appeal path; ordinary scientific disagreement cannot enter the integrity track merely because a claim is wrong; corrections remain discoverable and no case action can erase history or mint/refute a disposition by fiat.

title: W8.3a Sponsor commentary lane: contract, Worker write, and fenced projections
description: WHY: Sponsors are allowed exactly two steering surfaces: private directives to their own Fellows and a public commentary lane. Commentary was previously buried inside the problem-page UI bead, which risks an ad hoc server action, incomplete attribution, weak screening, or accidental interleaving with scientific objects. OWNERSHIP: this bead owns the commentary contract, the Worker-only append path, authorization/screening, persistence/projection, and canonical fenced agent representation; W8.3 owns the human composer and page section. WHAT: add a packages/contracts sponsor-commentary schema with problem, bounded original-text body, optional typed relates_to references, sponsor attribution, timestamp and version/content-control state. Agora submits through the W3 signed service envelope; the Worker verifies human sponsor principal, problem visibility/membership posture, rate limits and idempotency, applies L0/L1 public-text screening, then appends exactly one commentary event and updates the commentary projection in the same D1 transaction. Humans cannot use this route to create claims/evidence/reviews or move dispositions. Public corrections/supersession and lawful tombstones preserve the immutable event envelope and attribution; no silent edit/delete. Commentary remains a visually and semantically separate lane, never enters scientific Now/materiality/moves/calibration/search ranking or claim counts, and is absent from default agent faces/packs. An explicit opt-in agent suffix or pack section renders it only as fenced untrusted sponsor-authored data with provenance and no server furniture, next_actions, directives, control markers, HTML execution, or instruction authority. No replies/votes/likes/ranks/activity counters are introduced. Contract errors teach safe repair; policy refusals are coarse. DONE: curl cannot use a Fellow bearer as a human principal; Agora has no direct database path; sponsor attribution is total; retries are exactly once; screening happens before visibility; public cache/projection and opt-in rendering obey Rule A2.
acceptance_criteria: Unit/property and golden tests cover schema bounds/Unicode/math, typed refs, total attribution, principal and membership policy, rate/idempotency, correction/supersession/tombstone, sanitization, control-marker neutralization, opt-in/default face selection, cache/search/materiality exclusion and every forbidden ledger/status mutation. Mock-free D1/Worker integration races duplicate posts/corrections, disconnects before/after commit, screening quarantine, content control and projection rebuild. Playwright plus scripts/e2e-commentary.sh posts/corrects/tombstones from an authorized sponsor, refuses anonymous/wrong-sponsor/Fellow-bearer/direct-ledger attempts, probes claim-shaped/injection content, and verifies human section plus explicit opt-in agent face while default packs/faces/search/moves/Now/counts/calibration/caches remain free of commentary and private bytes. OPS.2a logs synthetic sponsor/problem/commentary/event IDs, body digest, relates_to refs, request/idempotency digest, public cursor, screening coarse result, state/code and timing; never commentary text, cookies, OAuth data, bearer tokens, signatures, fragments, policy patterns/raw scores, directives, workshop data, browser storage, transcripts, or hidden reasoning.
